source.original_text: The exact time of birth with the actual number of Vighatikas elapsed as revealed by foot-measurement or by the gnomonic shadow should first be specially ascertained. Then the positions of the planets coincident with observation should be set down with the help of mathematical instruments. Then the Bhavas and the strength of planets should be investigated and through them the effects should be judged.

interpretation.detailed: Step 1: Determine the exact time of birth using Vighatikas (a subdivison of time equal to 24 seconds) as measured by foot-measurement (a traditional time-keeping method based on the length of shadow cast by feet) or gnomonic shadow apparatus or equivalent instruments. Step 2: Compute and record the planetary positions for that exact moment using mathematical/astronomical methods. Step 3: Investigate the Bhavas (12 houses) and the strength (Bala) of each planet at the moment of birth. Step 4: Judge the effects (Phala) of the chart through the combined analysis of house positions and planetary strengths. This four-step sequence is the foundational methodology for all chart judgments in Phaladeepika. Correct astrological judgment proceeds from exact birth time → planetary positions → Bhava and strength analysis → effect pronouncement
interpretation.summary: The correct method for astrological judgment: (1) ascertain exact birth time in Vighatikas, (2) compute planetary positions, (3) investigate Bhavas and planetary strengths, (4) judge effects through them.

condition.description: Procedure for birth chart preparation and astrological judgment

source.original_text: The 3rd, the 6th, the 12th and the 8th houses are termed Leena Sthanas (concealed or hidden houses).

interpretation.detailed: Leena Sthanas (literally 'concealed/hidden positions') are the 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 12th houses. These four houses share the quality of hiddenness, secrecy, or concealment in the matters they govern. Note: three of these four (6th, 8th, 12th) are also Dusthanas (evil houses per sloka 17). The 3rd house is Leena but not classified as a Dusthana in this text. Houses 3, 6, 8, 12 = Leena Sthanas (concealed/hidden houses)
interpretation.summary: The 3rd, 6th, 8th, and 12th houses are classified as Leena Sthanas (concealed or hidden houses).

condition.description: House classification: Leena Sthanas

source.original_text: The 8th, the 6th and the 12th houses are known as Dusthanas (houses of evil).

interpretation.detailed: Dusthanas (literally 'bad places' or 'evil houses') are the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses. Planets placed in these houses or lords associated with these houses are considered inauspicious in their significations. These three houses govern enemies (6th), death and obstacles (8th), and losses and foreign lands (12th). The Dusthana classification is foundational for evaluating planetary placement quality throughout the book. Houses 6, 8, 12 = Dusthanas (evil/inauspicious houses)
interpretation.summary: The 6th, 8th, and 12th houses are classified as Dusthanas — houses of evil, inauspicious in nature.

condition.description: House classification: Dusthanas (evil houses)

source.original_text: The rest are termed good houses and will be propitious to the native.

interpretation.detailed: The nine houses that are not Dusthanas — 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 9th, 10th, 11th — are classified as good/propitious houses. Planets placed in these houses are generally in a favorable position for delivering benefic results, subject to other modifying factors. This is the broadest positive house classification in the text. Houses 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 = good/propitious houses
interpretation.summary: All houses other than the Dusthanas (6th, 8th, 12th) are classified as good houses — propitious to the native.

condition.description: House classification: good/propitious houses (non-Dusthanas)

source.original_text: The 1st, the 10th, the 7th and the 4th houses are known by the terms Kendra, Kantaka and Chatushtaya.

interpretation.detailed: Kendra houses (also called Kantaka — 'thorns/pillars' — and Chatushtaya — 'group of four') are the four angular houses: 1st (Lagna/Ascendant), 4th (Sukha/happiness), 7th (Jamitra/partnership), and 10th (Karma/action). Kendras are the most powerful house positions in Vedic astrology. Planets in Kendras are strong and their lords are especially significant. The Kendra classification is used throughout the book for yoga formulation, strength assessment, and house-lord analysis. Houses 1, 4, 7, 10 = Kendras (angular houses, also Kantaka/Chatushtaya)
interpretation.summary: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses are classified as Kendras (angles). Also known as Kantaka and Chatushtaya.

condition.description: House classification: Kendra (angular) houses

source.original_text: The houses next to the Kendras, i.e., the 2nd, the 5th, the 8th and the 11th are known as Panaphara.

interpretation.detailed: Panaphara houses (succedent houses, literally 'those following the Kendras') are the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th. They follow immediately after the four Kendra houses in the house sequence and are considered of intermediate strength — less powerful than Kendras but more powerful than Apoklima houses. In the Bala (planetary strength) assessment, planets in Panaparas deliver about half the results of planets in Kendras. Houses 2, 5, 8, 11 = Panaphara (succedent houses)
interpretation.summary: The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses — those immediately following the Kendras — are classified as Panaphara (succedent) houses.

condition.description: House classification: Panaphara (succedent) houses

source.original_text: The 3rd, the 6th, the 9th and the 12th are Apoklima houses.

interpretation.detailed: Apoklima houses (cadent houses, literally 'those falling away from the Kendras') are the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th. They are furthest from the angles and are considered the weakest house positions for planetary placement in terms of directional strength (Digbala). Planets in Apoklima houses deliver about one-quarter the results of planets in Kendras. Note: the 9th house is Apoklima in this classification but also a Trikona — the Trikona classification overrides for benefic assessment. Houses 3, 6, 9, 12 = Apoklima (cadent houses)
interpretation.summary: The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses are classified as Apoklima (cadent) houses.

condition.description: House classification: Apoklima (cadent) houses

source.original_text: The 4th and the 8th are designated Chaturasra houses.

interpretation.detailed: Chaturasra houses (literally 'square/quadrangular') are the 4th and 8th. This is an additional classification that overlaps with the other systems: the 4th is also a Kendra, while the 8th is also a Dusthana and a Panaphara. The Chaturasra classification specifically marks these two houses for their association with karmic/fixed matters — property and heritage (4th) and longevity and transformation (8th). Houses 4 and 8 = Chaturasra (square) houses
interpretation.summary: The 4th and 8th houses are classified as Chaturasra (square) houses.

condition.description: House classification: Chaturasra (square) houses

source.original_text: The 10th, the 3rd, the 6th and the 11th houses are called Upachaya.

interpretation.detailed: Upachaya houses (literally 'houses of increase/growth') are the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th. These houses are notable because malefic planets placed here are considered to give progressively better results over time — malefics improve in Upachaya houses. The 10th is also a Kendra; the 3rd and 6th are also Apoklima. The 6th is both Upachaya and Dusthana — its Upachaya nature means adversities (enemies, disease, debt) signified by malefics here can be overcome and defeated. Houses 3, 6, 10, 11 = Upachaya (growth) houses
interpretation.summary: The 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses are classified as Upachaya (houses of growth/increase).

condition.description: House classification: Upachaya (growth) houses

source.original_text: The 9th and the 5th are known as Trikona (triangular) houses and these are auspicious.

interpretation.detailed: Trikona houses (literally 'triangular houses', forming a trine with the Lagna) are the 5th and 9th. These two houses are explicitly declared auspicious (subha) in this sloka. Along with the Lagna (1st house, which also forms a trine), the 5th and 9th constitute the Dharma Trikona (triad of righteousness and fortune). Trikona lords are considered highly benefic even when they rule other signs. The 9th is simultaneously Trikona and Apoklima — the Trikona auspicious nature predominates for interpretive purposes. Houses 5 and 9 = Trikona (triangular) houses; explicitly auspicious
interpretation.summary: The 5th and 9th houses are classified as Trikona (triangular) houses and explicitly declared auspicious.

condition.description: House classification: Trikona (triangular/auspicious) houses

interpretation.detailed: Planets are mutually friendly for the time being when they occupy the 3rd, the 4th, the 2nd, the 10th, the 12th and the 11th from one another. This temporary friendship is combined with the natural friendship or enmity to determine the net relationship: both friendly = very friendly; both inimical = very inimical; one friendly one neutral = friendly; one inimical one neutral = inimical; etc.
interpretation.summary: Two planets placed in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 10th, 11th or 12th from each other are considered mutually friendly on a temporary basis.

interpretation.detailed: Saturn casts a full (100%) aspect on the 3rd house from its natal position. This is a special aspect unique to Saturn — beyond the universal 7th house aspect shared by all planets. The 3rd house aspect of Saturn is equal in strength to a 7th house aspect.
interpretation.summary: Saturn casts a full special aspect on the 3rd house in addition to the standard 7th house aspect.

interpretation.detailed: Saturn casts a full (100%) aspect on the 10th house from its natal position. This is a special aspect unique to Saturn, equal in strength to a 7th house aspect. The 10th house receives Saturn's direct influence regardless of its natal house placement.
interpretation.summary: Saturn casts a full special aspect on the 10th house in addition to the standard 7th house aspect.

interpretation.detailed: Jupiter casts a full (100%) aspect on the 5th house from its natal position. This special aspect is unique to Jupiter and is equal in strength to the 7th house aspect. Jupiter's 5th house aspect is auspicious for children, intelligence, past-life merit, and creative intelligence.
interpretation.summary: Jupiter casts a full special aspect on the 5th house in addition to the standard 7th house aspect.

interpretation.detailed: Jupiter casts a full (100%) aspect on the 9th house from its natal position. This special aspect is unique to Jupiter, equal in strength to the 7th house aspect. Jupiter's 9th house aspect is particularly auspicious for dharma, father, guru, fortune, and higher learning.
interpretation.summary: Jupiter casts a full special aspect on the 9th house in addition to the standard 7th house aspect.

interpretation.detailed: Mars casts a full (100%) aspect on the 4th house from its natal position. This special aspect is unique to Mars, equal in strength to the 7th house aspect. Mars's 4th house aspect affects the home, mother, landed property, and emotional security.
interpretation.summary: Mars casts a full special aspect on the 4th house in addition to the standard 7th house aspect.

interpretation.detailed: Mars casts a full (100%) aspect on the 8th house from its natal position. This special aspect is unique to Mars, equal in strength to the 7th house aspect. Mars's 8th house aspect affects longevity, hidden matters, transformation, and chronic health issues.
interpretation.summary: Mars casts a full special aspect on the 8th house in addition to the standard 7th house aspect.

interpretation.detailed: All planets universally cast aspects of the following strengths from their natal position: quarter (25%) strength at the 3rd and 10th houses; half (50%) strength at the 5th and 9th houses; three-quarters (75%) strength at the 4th and 8th houses; and full (100%) strength at the 7th house. Saturn, Jupiter and Mars additionally cast full-strength special aspects (see rules pd-ch02-002 through pd-ch02-007).
interpretation.summary: All planets cast aspects of varying strength: quarter at 3rd/10th, half at 5th/9th, three-quarters at 4th/8th, full at 7th.

interpretation.detailed: Mercury is a natural benefic by default. However, when Mercury is in conjunction with any natural malefic — the waning Moon, the Sun, Mars, Rahu, Ketu, or Saturn — Mercury too becomes malignant and acts as a malefic. This applies regardless of the house Mercury occupies. A benefic Mercury in conjunction with Jupiter or Venus retains its benefic nature.
interpretation.summary: Mercury loses its natural benefic quality and acts as a malefic when in conjunction with any natural malefic planet.

condition.configuration: Mercury in conjunction with any one or more of: waning Moon, Sun, Mars, Rahu, Ketu, Saturn

interpretation.detailed: When Rahu is prominent in the nativity (in the Lagna or strongly influencing the Lagna or its lord), the person born under its influence will be black in colour and tall in stature. These are Rahu's own physical characteristics reflected in the native.
interpretation.summary: A person born strongly under Rahu's influence will have a black complexion and tall stature.

interpretation.detailed: When Rahu is prominent in the nativity, the native suffers from skin disease, leprosy, and itch-cough (chronic cough or respiratory ailment). These are Rahu-specific health afflictions that manifest especially during Rahu dasha or when Rahu afflicts the Lagna or the 6th/8th house.
interpretation.summary: A person born strongly under Rahu's influence is prone to skin diseases, leprosy, and chronic respiratory conditions.

interpretation.detailed: When Rahu is prominent in the nativity, the person born under its influence is a heretic (against mainstream religious faith), speaks falsehood habitually, is cunning and deceitful, reviles and slanders others, and is devoid of sound intelligence. These Rahu character traits are especially pronounced when Rahu occupies or aspects the Lagna.
interpretation.summary: A person born strongly under Rahu's influence is heretical, deceptive, cunning, unintelligent, and given to reviling others.

interpretation.detailed: When Rahu is prominent in the nativity, the native is born of low caste or occupies low social standing in the traditional hierarchy. Rahu is itself associated with outcast and mleccha communities. This influence is mitigated if Rahu is well-aspected by Jupiter.
interpretation.summary: A person born strongly under Rahu's influence is of low social standing or low caste.

interpretation.detailed: When Ketu is prominent in the nativity, the person born under its influence has a red and fierce look, a smoky complexion, and an elevated (tall) body. The native carries an armed or militant appearance. These are Ketu's own physical characteristics reflected in the native when Ketu occupies or strongly influences the Lagna.
interpretation.summary: A person born strongly under Ketu's influence has a red fierce look, smoky colour, elevated body, and an armed/warrior bearing.

interpretation.detailed: When Ketu is prominent in the nativity, the native has bruised or damaged limbs, a thin lean body, and a disposition toward inhaling smoke (indicating lung, breathing, or chest-related afflictions). These Ketu-specific health conditions are most pronounced during Ketu dasha.
interpretation.summary: A person born strongly under Ketu's influence has bruised or injured limbs, a lean body, and respiratory issues related to smoke.

interpretation.detailed: When Ketu is prominent in the nativity, the native has a venomous tongue (harsh, wounding speech) and is malicious in nature. Ketu natives are prone to causing harm through words and intent. The always-inhaling-smoke quality also suggests ascetic or renunciatory tendencies alongside the malicious character.
interpretation.summary: A person born strongly under Ketu's influence has a venomous or sharp tongue and a malicious, spiteful disposition.

interpretation.detailed: When Ketu is prominent in the nativity, the native is considered an outcast (outcaste in the traditional varna hierarchy) and carries an armed or militant bearing. Ketu is associated with unconventional, fringe, or renunciate social positions. This social exclusion is a defining characteristic of strong Ketu influence on the Lagna.
interpretation.summary: A person born strongly under Ketu's influence is socially an outcast with a militant or armed bearing.

interpretation.detailed: Planets are said to be badly placed when they are: (1) eclipsed (combust, within Sun's combustion range); (2) debilitated — occupying their depression sign or a depression Navamsa (Amsa); (3) posited in the house of an enemy; or (4) occupying the 6th, 8th or 12th house (the Dusthanas). In any of these four conditions, the planet is weakened and produces adverse results.
interpretation.summary: A planet is considered badly placed when eclipsed, in its depression sign/Amsa, in an enemy's house, or in the 6th, 8th or 12th house.

interpretation.detailed: A planet is considered well-placed in all positions other than those of a badly placed planet — i.e., when it is not eclipsed (combust), not in depression sign or Amsa, not in an enemy's house, and not in the 6th, 8th or 12th house. In these other positions the planet produces its full and auspicious results.
interpretation.summary: A planet is well-placed when it is not eclipsed, not debilitated, not in an enemy's house, and not in the 6th, 8th or 12th house.

source.original_text: In the Rasi the effect is full; in the other Vargas (Hora, Drekkana etc.) it is half; in the Shodasamsa, Dasamsa and Shashtyamsa it is only a quarter.

interpretation.detailed: When computing a planet's combined varga strength, the Rasi (D1) contributes full weight. All intermediate divisional charts (Hora D2, Drekkana D3, Navamsa D9, Saptamsa D7, Dwadasamsa D12, Trimsamsa D30) contribute half weight. The finer varga charts — Shodasamsa (D16), Dasamsa (D10), and Shashtyamsa (D60) — contribute only one-quarter weight. Rasi = full weight; Hora/Drekkana/Navamsa/Saptamsa/Dwadasamsa/Trimsamsa = half weight; Shodasamsa/Dasamsa/Shashtyamsa = quarter weight
interpretation.summary: A planet's effect is fullest in its Rasi placement; halved in Hora/Drekkana/Navamsa/Saptamsa/Dwadasamsa/Trimsamsa; reduced to one-quarter in Shodasamsa, Dasamsa, and Shashtyamsa.

condition.description: Calculating weighted varga contribution of a planet across divisional charts

source.original_text: In odd signs: 1st 6 degrees = infancy; 2nd 6 = boyhood; 3rd 6 = adolescence; 4th 6 = advanced age; last 6 = extremis.

interpretation.detailed: For planets in odd signs, divide the sign into five 6-degree bands. A planet in 0-6 is in Balavastha (infancy); 6-12 is Kumaravastha (boyhood); 12-18 is Yuvavastha (adolescence/youth); 18-24 is Vridhavastha (advanced age); 24-30 is Mritavastha (extremis). These states affect how strongly the planet delivers results, per Sloka 20 proportionality rule. Planet Avastha assigned based on degree band in odd sign; affects proportional delivery of results
interpretation.summary: In odd signs (Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, Aquarius) a planet's Avastha is: 0-6 infancy, 6-12 boyhood, 12-18 adolescence, 18-24 advanced age, 24-30 extremis.

source.original_text: In even signs the order is reversed.

interpretation.detailed: For planets in even signs, the five Avastha states run in reverse order. 0-6 is Mritavastha (extremis); 6-12 is Vridhavastha (advanced age); 12-18 is Yuvavastha (adolescence); 18-24 is Kumaravastha (boyhood); 24-30 is Balavastha (infancy). A planet at 25 in an even sign is therefore in its youngest/most vigorous Avastha state. Planet Avastha assigned in reverse degree order for even signs
interpretation.summary: In even signs (Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, Pisces) the Avastha sequence reverses: 0-6 extremis, 6-12 advanced age, 12-18 adolescence, 18-24 boyhood, 24-30 infancy.

source.original_text: If a planet is in its own, exaltation, or friendly house in 2 Vargas — Parijatamsa: the native will be respectable, have good qualities, wealth, happiness, power and dignity.

interpretation.detailed: Parijatamsa is the first Vaiseshikamsa dignity level. A planet achieves Parijatamsa when placed in its own sign, sign of exaltation, or friendly sign in 2 out of the 10 Dasavarga charts (D1, D2, D3, D7, D9, D10, D12, D16, D30, D60). Native born with such a planet: respectable, endowed with good qualities, wealth, happiness, power, and dignity. Native is respectable, has good qualities, wealth, happiness, power, and dignity
interpretation.summary: Planet in own/exaltation/friendly sign in 2 of 10 Dasavarga charts = Parijatamsa. Native: respectable, good qualities, wealth, happiness, power, dignity.

source.original_text: In 3 Vargas — Uttamamsa: modest, clever, good behaviour.

interpretation.detailed: Uttamamsa is the second Vaiseshikamsa dignity level. A planet achieves Uttamamsa when it occupies its own, exaltation, or friendly sign in 3 out of the 10 Dasavarga charts. The native will be modest in character, clever/intelligent, and of good behaviour. Native is modest, clever, and of good behaviour
interpretation.summary: Planet in own/exaltation/friendly sign in 3 of 10 Dasavarga charts = Uttamamsa. Native: modest, clever, good behaviour.

source.original_text: In 4 Vargas — Gopuramsa: good intellect, wealth, lands, cattle, house.

interpretation.detailed: Gopuramsa is the third Vaiseshikamsa dignity level. A planet achieves Gopuramsa when placed in own, exaltation, or friendly sign in 4 of the 10 Dasavarga charts. The native will have good intellect, wealth, lands (property), cattle (livestock), and a house (real estate). Native has good intellect, wealth, lands, cattle, and a house
interpretation.summary: Planet in own/exaltation/friendly sign in 4 of 10 Dasavarga charts = Gopuramsa. Native: good intellect, wealth, lands, cattle, house.

source.original_text: In 5 Vargas — Simhasanamsa: friend of a king, or his equal.

interpretation.detailed: Simhasanamsa is the fourth Vaiseshikamsa dignity level. A planet achieves Simhasanamsa when placed in own, exaltation, or friendly sign in 5 of the 10 Dasavarga charts. The native will be a friend of a king or equal to royalty in status and privilege. Native is a friend of a king or equal to a king in status
interpretation.summary: Planet in own/exaltation/friendly sign in 5 of 10 Dasavarga charts = Simhasanamsa. Native: friend of a king, or equal to a king.

source.original_text: In 6 Vargas — Paravatamsa: very good horses, elephants, vehicles, princely appendages.

interpretation.detailed: Paravatamsa is the fifth Vaiseshikamsa dignity level. A planet achieves Paravatamsa when placed in own, exaltation, or friendly sign in 6 of the 10 Dasavarga charts. The native will possess very fine horses, elephants, vehicles, and the princely accessories befitting high status. Native possesses very fine horses, elephants, vehicles, and princely appendages
interpretation.summary: Planet strong in 6 of 10 Dasavarga charts = Paravatamsa. Native: very fine horses, elephants, vehicles, and princely appendages.

source.original_text: In 7 Vargas — Devalokamsa: King widely renowned for good qualities.

interpretation.detailed: Devalokamsa is the sixth Vaiseshikamsa dignity level. A planet achieves Devalokamsa when placed in own, exaltation, or friendly sign in 7 of the 10 Dasavarga charts. The native will be a king widely renowned for good qualities — combining sovereign power with an excellent reputation. Native is a king widely renowned for good qualities
interpretation.summary: Planet strong in 7 of 10 Dasavarga charts = Devalokamsa. Native: king widely renowned for good qualities.

source.original_text: In 8 Vargas — Suralokamsa: good luck, wealth, corn, children, kingship.

interpretation.detailed: Suralokamsa is the seventh Vaiseshikamsa dignity level. A planet achieves Suralokamsa when placed in own, exaltation, or friendly sign in 8 of the 10 Dasavarga charts. The native will enjoy excellent luck, great wealth, abundance of corn/food, many children, and kingship. Native has good luck, wealth, abundance, many children, and kingship
interpretation.summary: Planet strong in 8 of 10 Dasavarga charts = Suralokamsa. Native: good luck, wealth, abundance, children, kingship.

source.original_text: In 9 Vargas — Airavatamsa: Equal to God Indra; saluted by kings.

interpretation.detailed: Airavatamsa is the eighth and highest Vaiseshikamsa dignity level. A planet achieves Airavatamsa when placed in own, exaltation, or friendly sign in 9 of the 10 Dasavarga charts. The native born with such a planet is equal to the god Indra (king of gods) in status and is saluted/honoured by kings. Native is equal to God Indra in status; saluted by kings
interpretation.summary: Planet strong in 9 of 10 Dasavarga charts = Airavatamsa (highest tier). Native: equal to God Indra; saluted by kings.

source.original_text: A planet weak in all 10 Vargas — death of the native.

interpretation.detailed: The inverse of Vaiseshikamsa: when a planet fails to occupy own, exaltation, or friendly sign in any of the 10 Dasavarga charts (total varga weakness = 10/10), this extreme debility corresponds to death of the native. This is the most severe outcome in the varga weakness scale. Death of the native
interpretation.summary: A planet in enemy/debilitation sign in all 10 Dasavarga charts indicates death of the native.

source.original_text: Weak in 9 Vargas — destruction.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet is in an unfriendly, debilitation, or enemy sign in 9 of 10 Dasavarga charts, this near-total weakness corresponds to destruction — severe ruin of the significations associated with that planet. Destruction
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in 9 of 10 Dasavarga charts indicates destruction for the native.

source.original_text: Weak in 8 Vargas — grief.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet is in an unfriendly or debilitated sign in 8 of 10 Dasavarga charts, this high varga weakness corresponds to grief — persistent sorrow and distress related to the planet's significations. Grief
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in 8 of 10 Dasavarga charts indicates grief for the native.

source.original_text: Weak in 7 Vargas — calamity.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet is in an unfriendly or debilitated sign in 7 of 10 Dasavarga charts, this degree of varga weakness corresponds to calamity — a severe adverse event affecting the native in areas ruled by that planet. Calamity
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in 7 of 10 Dasavarga charts indicates calamity for the native.

source.original_text: Weak in 6 Vargas — unhappiness.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet is in an unfriendly or debilitated sign in 6 of 10 Dasavarga charts, this moderate-high varga weakness corresponds to general unhappiness and dissatisfaction in the planet's signification areas. Unhappiness
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in 6 of 10 Dasavarga charts indicates unhappiness for the native.

source.original_text: Weak in 5 Vargas — calamity among relations.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet is in an unfriendly or debilitated sign in 5 of 10 Dasavarga charts, this mid-level varga weakness corresponds to calamity among relations — misfortune befalling family members or close associates rather than the native directly. Calamity among relations
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in 5 of 10 Dasavarga charts indicates calamity among the native's relations.

source.original_text: Weak in 4 Vargas — love of (loss of) relatives.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet is in an unfriendly or debilitated sign in 4 of 10 Dasavarga charts, this weakness corresponds to loss of relatives — bereavement or separation from family members. Some commentators read this as concern/love for relatives who suffer; others read it as actual loss. Both meanings are retained here. Loss of relatives
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in 4 of 10 Dasavarga charts indicates loss of relatives (bereavement or separation from family).

source.original_text: Weak in 3 Vargas — friend of a king.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet is in an unfriendly or debilitated sign in only 3 of 10 Dasavarga charts (strong in the remaining 7), this relatively mild varga weakness still yields a positive outcome: the native will be a friend of a king, enjoying royal patronage and association with power. Friend of a king
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in only 3 of 10 Dasavarga charts (strong in 7) — native will be a friend of a king.

source.original_text: Weak in 2 Vargas — wealthy man.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet occupies an unfriendly or debilitated sign in only 2 of 10 Dasavarga charts (predominantly strong), the native benefits with wealth — financial prosperity and material comfort in the signification areas of that planet. Wealthy man
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in only 2 of 10 Dasavarga charts (strong in 8) — native will be a wealthy man.

source.original_text: Weak in 1 Varga — king.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet occupies an unfriendly or debilitated sign in only 1 of 10 Dasavarga charts (strong in 9), the planet has near-maximal varga strength and the native will be a king — a ruler or sovereign. King
interpretation.summary: A planet weak in only 1 of 10 Dasavarga charts (strong in 9) — native will be a king.

source.original_text: Strong in all 10 Vargas — best among kings.

interpretation.detailed: When a planet occupies its own, exaltation, or friendly sign in all 10 Dasavarga charts — total varga strength — the native will be the best among kings, a paramount sovereign above all other rulers. This is distinct from Airavatamsa (strong in 9 of 10) and represents absolute maximum varga strength. Best among kings
interpretation.summary: A planet strong in all 10 Dasavarga charts (not weak in any) — native will be the best among kings.

source.original_text: 1st state (Bala/infancy) — native progressing.

interpretation.detailed: The first of five degree-based Avastha states. When a planet occupies the degree band corresponding to Balavastha (infancy) per the odd/even sign degree rules of Sloka 3, the planet's significations manifest as the native being in a state of progress or improvement. Benefic results are beginning to develop but are not yet full. Native is progressing
interpretation.summary: A planet in Balavastha (infancy, 1st of 5 degree states) gives an outcome where the native is progressing/improving.

source.original_text: 2nd state — native happy.

interpretation.detailed: The second of five degree-based Avastha states. When a planet occupies the degree band corresponding to Kumaravastha (boyhood), the native experiences happiness and positive emotional states in the areas signified by that planet. Native is happy
interpretation.summary: A planet in Kumaravastha (boyhood, 2nd of 5 degree states) gives an outcome where the native is happy.

source.original_text: 3rd state (middle) — native like a king.

interpretation.detailed: The third of five degree-based Avastha states and the peak of planetary strength in a sign. When a planet occupies the degree band corresponding to Yuvavastha (adolescence/youth), the planet is at its strongest and the native lives like a king — enjoying authority, power, and the fullest expression of its significations. Native like a king
interpretation.summary: A planet in Yuvavastha (adolescence, 3rd of 5 degree states) — the peak state — gives an outcome where the native is like a king.

source.original_text: 4th state — native suffering from disease.

interpretation.detailed: The fourth of five degree-based Avastha states. When a planet occupies the degree band corresponding to Vridhavastha (advanced age/old age), the planet's weakening is reflected as health affliction — the native experiences illness or disease in the matters signified by that planet. Native suffers from disease
interpretation.summary: A planet in Vridhavastha (advanced age, 4th of 5 degree states) gives an outcome where the native suffers from disease.

source.original_text: 5th state (Mrita/extremis) — native as if dead.

interpretation.detailed: The fifth and weakest of the five degree-based Avastha states. When a planet occupies the degree band corresponding to Mritavastha (extremis/death-like), the planet is at its lowest vitality and the native is as if dead — extremely diminished in the areas signified by that planet, with near-nil results from that planet's significations. Native as if dead — planet gives near-nil results
interpretation.summary: A planet in Mritavastha (extremis, 5th of 5 degree states) — the weakest state — gives an outcome where the native is as if dead.

source.original_text: Benefic planets preponderant in Shadvargas — very wealthy, long-lived.

interpretation.detailed: When the majority of the six Shadvarga charts (Rasi, Hora, Drekkana, Navamsa, Dwadasamsa, Trimsamsa) show benefic placements for the planet(s), the native benefits with great wealth and long life. The Shadvarga benefic preponderance represents a holistic positive varga profile. Very wealthy and long-lived
interpretation.summary: When benefic planets are preponderant (majority) across the six Shadvargas (D1, D2, D3, D9, D12, D30), the native will be very wealthy and long-lived.

condition.description: Benefic planets preponderant across Shadvargas (D1/D2/D3/D9/D12/D30)

source.original_text: Lagna in Krura Amsas (Shadvargas) — poor, short-lived, wicked.

interpretation.detailed: When the Lagna occupies Krura (cruel, malefic-owned) Amsas across the Shadvargas — i.e., falls in divisional positions belonging to natural malefics — the native will be poor, short-lived, and of wicked or sinful character. This is the negative counterpart of the benefic preponderance rule. Poor, short-lived, and wicked
interpretation.summary: When the Lagna (Ascendant) falls in Krura (cruel/malefic) divisional positions across the Shadvargas, the native will be poor, short-lived, and wicked.

condition.description: Lagna falls in Krura (malefic-owned) Amsas across Shadvargas

source.original_text: Exception: lords of those Krura Amsas are strong — becomes king.

interpretation.detailed: When the Lagna is in Krura Amsas across Shadvargas (normally indicating poverty and short life), if the lords of those very Krura Amsas are themselves strong and well-placed, the negative outcome is reversed and the native becomes a king. This is a classic cancellation/override principle in Vedic astrology. Native becomes a king (overrides poverty/short-life outcome)
interpretation.summary: Exception to pd-ch03-029: if the lords of those Krura Amsas are strong, the native becomes a king instead of being poor/short-lived.

condition.description: Lagna in Krura Amsas AND lords of those Krura Amsas are strong

source.original_text: Rising Navamsa lord strong — happiness and comfort.

interpretation.detailed: The rising Navamsa is the sign of the Navamsa (D9) chart that was on the eastern horizon at birth. When the lord of this rising Navamsa sign is strong (well-placed, in own/exaltation/friendly sign, or aspected beneficially), the native will enjoy happiness and comfort in life. Native enjoys happiness and comfort
interpretation.summary: When the lord of the rising Navamsa (the sign rising in D9 at birth) is strong, the native will enjoy happiness and comfort.

condition.description: Lord of rising Navamsa sign is strong

source.original_text: Rising Drekkana lord strong — equal to a king.

interpretation.detailed: The rising Drekkana is the sign of the Drekkana (D3) chart that was on the eastern horizon at birth. When the lord of this rising Drekkana sign is strong, the native will enjoy status and power equal to a king — sovereign-like authority and prestige. Native is equal to a king
interpretation.summary: When the lord of the rising Drekkana (the decanate sign rising in D3 at birth) is strong, the native will be equal to a king.

condition.description: Lord of rising Drekkana sign is strong

source.original_text: Rising Lagna Rasi lord strong — ruler of Earth with good fortune.

interpretation.detailed: When the lord of the Lagna (Ascendant, D1) is strong — placed in own sign, exaltation, or a strong house, or aspected by benefics — the native will be a ruler of the Earth, endowed with all good fortune. This is the highest outcome among the three rising divisional lord rules in this sloka. Native is a ruler of the Earth with good fortune
interpretation.summary: When the lord of the rising Lagna Rasi (Ascendant sign lord) is strong, the native will be a ruler of the Earth with good fortune.

condition.description: Lord of rising Lagna Rasi (Ascendant lord) is strong

source.original_text: Malefics in Sun's Hora in odd Rasis — native strong, sturdy, cruel, wealthy.

interpretation.detailed: The Sun rules the first Hora (0-15 degrees) in odd signs. When malefic planets (Saturn, Mars, Rahu, Ketu, Sun) occupy the Sun's Hora in odd Rasis, the native born with such a configuration will be physically strong, sturdy in constitution, cruel or harsh in nature, and wealthy. The harsh qualities of both the malefics and the Sun's aggressive Hora combine to produce strength and cruelty alongside material prosperity. Native is strong, sturdy, cruel, and wealthy
interpretation.summary: When malefic planets occupy the Sun's Hora (first 15 degrees in odd signs, last 15 degrees in even signs) in odd Rasis, the native will be strong, sturdy, cruel, and wealthy.

source.original_text: Benefics in Moon's Hora in even signs — brilliant appearance, mild speech, pleasant, graceful.

interpretation.detailed: The Moon rules the second Hora (15-30 degrees) in odd signs and the first Hora (0-15 degrees) in even signs. When benefic planets (Jupiter, Venus, waxing Mercury, waxing Moon) occupy the Moon's Hora in even Rasis, the native will have a brilliant and attractive appearance, mild and gentle speech, a pleasant and agreeable manner, and overall grace and elegance. Native has brilliant appearance, mild speech, pleasant manner, and graceful disposition
interpretation.summary: When benefic planets occupy the Moon's Hora (last 15 degrees in odd signs, first 15 degrees in even signs) in even signs, the native will have brilliant appearance, mild speech, pleasant manner, and graceful disposition.

source.original_text: Lagna and Moon both very strong + their lords strong — long life, no sorrow, widely renowned.

interpretation.detailed: A three-part conjunction of strength: (1) the Lagna (Ascendant) is very strong, (2) the Moon is very strong, and (3) both the Lagna lord and the Moon's sign lord are strong. When all three conditions are met simultaneously, the native will enjoy long life, freedom from sorrow throughout life, and wide renown/fame. Long life, no sorrow, widely renowned
interpretation.summary: When the Lagna and Moon are both very strong AND their lords are also strong, the native will be long-lived, free from sorrow, and widely renowned.

source.original_text: Born with serpent or quadruped decanate rising — without wealth, cruel, vile character, indigent.

interpretation.detailed: Serpent decanates: first decanate of Vrischika (Scorpio), last of Karkataka (Cancer), last of Meena (Pisces). Quadruped decanates: 2nd of Mesha (Aries), 2nd of Vrishabha (Taurus), 1st of Simha (Leo), last of Vrischika (Scorpio). When the Lagna (Ascendant) falls in one of these decanates at birth, the native will be without wealth, cruel in temperament, of vile and low character, and generally indigent/impoverished. Without wealth, cruel, vile character, indigent
interpretation.summary: When a serpent-face or quadruped decanate is rising at birth (specific decanates in Scorpio, Cancer, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, Leo), the native will be without wealth, cruel, of vile character, and indigent.

condition.description: Lagna falls in serpent decanate (1st Scorpio, last Cancer, last Pisces) OR quadruped decanate (2nd Aries, 2nd Taurus, 1st Leo, last Scorpio)

source.original_text: Dual sign: 1st decanate = bad; 2nd = moderate; 3rd = good.

interpretation.detailed: In dual (Dwishwabhava/mutable) signs — Mithuna (Gemini), Kanya (Virgo), Dhanus (Sagittarius), Meena (Pisces) — the quality of the decanate rising at birth follows a progressive scale: 1st decanate (0-10 degrees) = bad/inauspicious results; 2nd decanate (10-20 degrees) = moderate/middling results; 3rd decanate (20-30 degrees) = good/auspicious results. 1st decanate = bad; 2nd decanate = moderate; 3rd decanate = good
interpretation.summary: In dual (mutable) signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), the 1st decanate is bad, 2nd is moderate, 3rd is good.

condition.description: Lagna in dual sign; decanate quality varies by 1st/2nd/3rd decanate

source.original_text: Moveable sign: 1st decanate = good; 2nd = moderate; 3rd = bad (reversed).

interpretation.detailed: In moveable (Chara/cardinal) signs — Mesha (Aries), Karkataka (Cancer), Tula (Libra), Makara (Capricorn) — the decanate quality is the reverse of the dual sign pattern: 1st decanate (0-10 degrees) = good/auspicious; 2nd decanate (10-20 degrees) = moderate; 3rd decanate (20-30 degrees) = bad/inauspicious. 1st decanate = good; 2nd decanate = moderate; 3rd decanate = bad
interpretation.summary: In moveable (cardinal) signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), the decanate quality is reversed: 1st good, 2nd moderate, 3rd bad.

condition.description: Lagna in moveable sign; decanate quality varies by 1st/2nd/3rd decanate

source.original_text: Fixed sign: 1st decanate = bad; 2nd = good; 3rd = mixed.

interpretation.detailed: In fixed (Sthira) signs — Vrishabha (Taurus), Simha (Leo), Vrischika (Scorpio), Kumbha (Aquarius) — the decanate quality pattern is: 1st decanate (0-10 degrees) = bad/inauspicious; 2nd decanate (10-20 degrees) = good/auspicious; 3rd decanate (20-30 degrees) = mixed (neither fully good nor fully bad). 1st decanate = bad; 2nd decanate = good; 3rd decanate = mixed
interpretation.summary: In fixed signs (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius), the decanate quality is: 1st bad, 2nd good, 3rd mixed.

condition.description: Lagna in fixed sign; decanate quality varies by 1st/2nd/3rd decanate

source.original_text: Rising decanate lord in own Varga, or aspected by benefic, or in exaltation/friendly house; AND rising Trimsamsa/Dwadasamsa/Hora lord similarly positioned — native: all good qualities, pure, clever, long-lived, merciful, wealthy, many children, widely renowned, royal-style comforts.

interpretation.detailed: A compound condition requiring strength in multiple rising divisional lords simultaneously. If the lord of the rising Drekkana (decanate) is (a) in its own Varga, or (b) aspected by a benefic, or (c) in exaltation or a friendly house — AND ALSO the lords of the rising Trimsamsa, Dwadasamsa, and Hora are similarly well-placed — then the native will possess all good qualities, be of pure character, clever/intelligent, long-lived, merciful, wealthy, blessed with many children, widely renowned, and enjoying royal-style comforts. All good qualities, pure, clever, long-lived, merciful, wealthy, many children, widely renowned, royal-style comforts
interpretation.summary: When the rising decanate lord is in own varga, benefic-aspected, or exalted/friendly, AND the rising Trimsamsa/Dwadasamsa/Hora lord is similarly strong, the native attains an outstanding royal-level outcome.

components: Rising Drekkana lord in own Varga OR benefic-aspected OR in exaltation/friendly house

source.original_text: Find Rasi of Mandi at birth. Lagna will be triangular to that lord's position; or triangular to Navamsa of owner of Mandi's Navamsa sign; or triangular to the Navamsa Rasi occupied by Gulika. When Moon is strong: use Moon instead of Mandi.

interpretation.detailed: This is a methodology rule for finding the Lagna (Ascendant) through Mandi (Gulika). Step 1: Identify the Rasi (sign) occupied by Mandi at birth. Step 2: Note the lord of that Rasi. Step 3: The Lagna will be one of the three signs that form a triangle (trine) to that lord's position (i.e., the 1st, 5th, or 9th from that lord). Alternative: Lagna will be triangular to the Navamsa sign of the lord who owns the sign of Mandi's Navamsa position. Or: triangular to the Navamsa Rasi actually occupied by Gulika. When the Moon is strong at birth, substitute the Moon for Mandi in all these calculations. Lagna identified as trine to Mandi's sign lord, or trine to Navamsa lord of Mandi's Navamsa sign, or trine to Gulika's Navamsa Rasi
interpretation.summary: Engine-spec rule for determining Lagna via Mandi: Lagna is trine to (a) lord of Mandi's Rasi, or (b) Navamsa lord of Mandi's Navamsa sign, or (c) Navamsa Rasi of Gulika. Moon substitutes for Mandi when Moon is strong.

condition.description: Determining Lagna via Mandi/Gulika triangular tracing method

source.original_text: Moon in own or friendly decanate — native beautiful, good qualities.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is placed in a decanate (Drekkana) that is either its own (the decanate whose lord is the Moon) or belongs to a planet friendly to the Moon, the native will be beautiful/attractive in appearance and endowed with good personal qualities and virtuous character. Native is beautiful and has good qualities
interpretation.summary: When the Moon occupies its own decanate or a friendly planet's decanate, the native will be beautiful and endowed with good qualities.

source.original_text: Moon in Uttamavarga — native very lucky.

interpretation.detailed: Uttamavarga refers to a planet being in a dignified position (own, exaltation, or friendly sign) across multiple divisional charts. When the Moon specifically attains Uttamavarga dignity, the native will be very lucky — enjoying an exceptionally fortunate and blessed life. Native is very lucky
interpretation.summary: When the Moon is in Uttamavarga (placed in its own, exaltation, or friendly sign in 3 or more of the varga charts), the native will be very lucky.

condition.description: Moon in Uttamavarga (strong in 3+ Vargas)

source.original_text: Planet in own Trimsamsa — produces full Karaka effects.

interpretation.detailed: The Trimsamsa (D30) chart governs a planet's ability to deliver its Karaka (significator) results. When a planet is placed in the Trimsamsa sign that it rules (its own Trimsamsa), it can deliver its full Karaka effects without diminishment. This is the maximum expression of a planet's natural significations. Planet produces full Karaka (significator) effects
interpretation.summary: When a planet occupies its own Trimsamsa (D30) sign, it produces its full Karaka (significator) effects for the native.

condition.description: Planet in its own Trimsamsa (D30) sign

source.original_text: At least one planet in exaltation/own house, aspected by friendly planet — native becomes king with riches.

interpretation.detailed: A two-part condition: (1) at least one planet in the chart occupies its sign of exaltation or its own sign, AND (2) that same planet receives the aspect of a friendly planet. When both conditions are met, the native becomes a king endowed with great riches. The friendly aspect amplifies and confirms the planet's strength, elevating its promise from merely strong to regal. Native becomes a king with riches
interpretation.summary: When at least one planet is in exaltation or own house AND that planet is aspected by a friendly planet, the native becomes a king with riches.

components: At least one planet in exaltation or own sign
That planet aspected by a friendly planet

source.original_text: Planet in Pradeeptavastha (blazing/exaltation state) — good effect is full.

interpretation.detailed: Pradeeptavastha (blazing state) is the highest of the named planetary Avasthas from Slokas 18-19. When a planet is in this state — typically when it is in its exaltation sign or at peak dignity — its beneficial effects are produced in their entirety without any reduction. Full Karaka and house results flow unimpeded. Good effects are full (undiminished)
interpretation.summary: When a planet is in Pradeeptavastha (the highest/blazing avastha, associated with exaltation strength), its good effects are delivered in full.

condition.description: Planet in Pradeeptavastha (blazing/highest avastha)

source.original_text: Planet in Vikala state (weakened/extremis) — effect is nil.

interpretation.detailed: Vikalavastha (also Mritavastha in the degree-based system) is the lowest of the named planetary Avasthas. When a planet is in this state — either due to its degree position (extremis band) or its overall debilitated/afflicted condition — it cannot produce any results whatsoever. Both benefic and malefic effects are suppressed to nil. Effect is nil — planet produces no results
interpretation.summary: When a planet is in Vikalavastha (the weakest/decimated avastha), its effects are nil — the planet cannot produce any result.

condition.description: Planet in Vikalavastha (weakest/decimated avastha)

source.original_text: Intervening Avasthas — good effects decrease and unpropitiousness increases proportionately.

interpretation.detailed: This is a proportionality rule for the full Avastha scale. Between the maximum (Pradeeptavastha = full good effect) and the minimum (Vikalavastha = nil effect), the intermediate Avasthas (Supta, Mudita, Shanta, Deena, Khal, Kopa — from Slokas 18-19) each represent a proportionate step down in good effects and a proportionate step up in adverse effects. The engine should interpolate effect magnitude accordingly based on which Avastha state the planet occupies. Good effects decrease proportionately; unpropitiousness increases proportionately as Avastha descends from Pradeeptavastha toward Vikalavastha
interpretation.summary: For Avasthas between Pradeeptavastha (full effect) and Vikalavastha (nil effect), good effects decrease proportionately and unpropitious effects increase proportionately with each descending state.

condition.description: Planet in any intermediate Avastha state between Pradeeptavastha and Vikalavastha

source.original_text: The strength of a planet is said to be sixfold: (1) Kalaja or temporal, (2) Cheshta or motional, (3) Ucchaja or that derived from its exaltation position, (4) Dik or directional, (5) Ayana or that derived from its declination and (6) Sthana or positional.

interpretation.detailed: The complete planetary strength system used in Phaladeepika is the Shadbala (literally 'six strengths'). The six components in order are: (1) Kalaja Bala — temporal strength based on time of birth, planetary periods, and day/night; (2) Cheshta Bala — motional strength based on the planet's movement (full moon, northern course, retrograde); (3) Ucchaja Bala — exaltation strength based on proximity to highest exaltation degree; (4) Dik Bala — directional strength based on house position; (5) Ayana Bala — declination strength based on north/south movement; (6) Sthana Bala — positional strength from varga placements and house type. All six are summed in Rupas to give total Shadbala. Shadbala = Kalaja + Cheshta + Ucchaja + Dik + Ayana + Sthana bala
interpretation.summary: Planetary strength (Shadbala) is sixfold: Kalaja (temporal), Cheshta (motional), Ucchaja (exaltation), Dik (directional), Ayana (declination), Sthana (positional).

condition.description: Definition of the six components of Shadbala

In day-time births, their Kalaja contribution from this component is reduced. Mars, Moon, Venus are temporally strong in night births

In night-time births their Kalaja contribution from this component is reduced. Sun, Jupiter, Saturn are temporally strong in day births

interpretation.summary: Mercury acquires Kalaja (temporal) strength at all times — both day and night.

interpretation.detailed: During the bright half of the lunar month (Shukla Paksha, from new moon to full moon), benefic planets — Jupiter, Venus, waxing Mercury, waxing Moon — acquire heightened Kalaja Bala. This Paksha-based component of temporal strength applies to birth charts based on the lunar phase at birth. Benefics are temporally strong in bright-half births
interpretation.summary: Benefic planets gain Kalaja (temporal) strength during the bright fortnight (Shukla Paksha, waxing moon).

source.original_text: In the dark-half the malefics are strong.

Birth during the dark fortnight enhances the Paksha-based temporal strength of malefics. Malefics are temporally strong in dark-half births
interpretation.summary: Malefic planets gain Kalaja (temporal) strength during the dark fortnight (Krishna Paksha, waning moon).

source.original_text: Planets when they happen to be the lords of the year, month, day and hour get 1, ½, ¼ and 1 Rupa respectively.

interpretation.detailed: As part of Kalaja Bala, when a planet rules the current time-period at the moment of birth, it gains additional Rupas: the lord of the solar year = 1 Rupa; the lord of the lunar month = ½ Rupa; the lord of the weekday = ¼ Rupa; the lord of the birth hour (Hora) = 1 Rupa. Note: the year lord and hour lord both get a full 1 Rupa, making birth-hour lordship as valuable as year lordship. Year lord = 1 Rupa; month lord = ½ Rupa; day lord = ¼ Rupa; hour lord = 1 Rupa
interpretation.summary: A planet that is the lord of the current year gets 1 Rupa; month lord gets ½ Rupa; day lord gets ¼ Rupa; hour (Hora) lord gets 1 Rupa of Kalaja Bala.

source.original_text: The Moon gets Cheshtabala when she is full. The Sun gets it when he is in his northern course; the other planets, when in their retrograde motion.

interpretation.detailed: Cheshta Bala (motional strength) is acquired under specific motion conditions: the Moon acquires it when she is full (Purnima — peak Pakshabala); the Sun acquires it when he is on his northern course (Uttarayana — Sun moving toward Cancer from Capricorn); all other planets (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn) acquire it when they are in retrograde motion (vakra gati). Full Cheshtabala corresponds to the highest motional state for each luminary. Moon full = Cheshtabala; Sun in Uttarayana = Cheshtabala; Mars/Mercury/Jupiter/Venus/Saturn retrograde = Cheshtabala
interpretation.summary: Cheshtabala (motional strength): Moon when full (Purnima); Sun when in northern course (Uttarayana); other five planets when retrograde.

source.original_text: In planetary war, those that are posited in the north and who have got brilliant rays should be considered as victorious.

interpretation.detailed: Grahayuddha (planetary war) occurs when two planets come within approximately 1 degree of each other in longitude. The victor is determined by two factors: (1) the planet positioned to the north (higher in declination) and (2) having more brilliant or brighter rays. The victorious planet retains its full strength and significations; the defeated planet loses strength and its significations are suppressed. North-positioned planet with brilliant rays = victor; retains full strength
interpretation.summary: In a planetary war (two planets within 1 degree), the planet that is positioned to the north AND has brighter/more brilliant rays is the victor.

condition.description: Two planets in Grahayuddha (within ~1 degree)

source.original_text: Planets have their full Uchchabala when in their highest exaltation.

interpretation.detailed: Uchchabala (exaltation strength) is proportional to how close a planet is to its highest exaltation degree. At the exact highest exaltation degree (e.g., Sun at 10° Aries, Moon at 3° Taurus, etc.), the planet has full Uchchabala = 60 Shashtiamsas = 1 Rupa. The strength decreases as the planet moves away from this degree, becoming nil at the depression degree (7th sign from exaltation, at the same degree). Planet has full Uchchabala (1 Rupa / 60 Shashtiamsas)
interpretation.summary: A planet's exaltation strength (Uchchabala) is at maximum when the planet occupies its exact highest exaltation degree.

condition.description: Planet at its highest exaltation degree

source.original_text: As regards directional strength, the Sun and Mars are strong in the 10th; Venus and the Moon in the 4th; Mercury and Jupiter in the 1st; and Saturn in the 7th.

interpretation.detailed: Digbala (directional strength) is the component of Shadbala based on which house a planet occupies. Each planet has one house where it achieves full Digbala (1 Rupa): Sun and Mars = 10th house (south/meridian, associated with action and power); Moon and Venus = 4th house (north/nadir, associated with comfort and beauty); Mercury and Jupiter = 1st house (east/ascendant, associated with intelligence and growth); Saturn = 7th house (west/descendant, associated with patience and separation). Digbala decreases as the planet moves away from its Digbala house. Full Digbala at assigned house; decreases proportionally with distance from Digbala house
interpretation.summary: Full directional strength (Digbala): Sun and Mars in 10th; Moon and Venus in 4th; Mercury and Jupiter in 1st; Saturn in 7th.

source.original_text: Mercury, Saturn and the Moon have their Ayana bala in their southerly course. The rest have the same in their northern.

interpretation.detailed: Ayana Bala (declination strength) is based on whether a planet is moving north or south in declination. Mercury, Saturn, and the Moon acquire Ayanabala when on their southerly (Dakshinayana) course. The Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Venus acquire Ayanabala when on their northerly (Uttarayana) course. This rule appears counterintuitive for the Moon since the Moon benefits from the southern declination while the Sun benefits from the northern — this is the standard Shadbala doctrine. Mercury/Saturn/Moon full Ayanabala in south; Sun/Mars/Jupiter/Venus full Ayanabala in north
interpretation.summary: Ayanabala (declination strength): Mercury, Saturn, and Moon gain it in their southerly declination course; Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Venus gain it in their northerly course.

source.original_text: The strength accruing to a planet in the six Vargas (Rasi, Hora, Drekkana, Navamsa, Dwadasamsa and Trimsamsa) on a consideration of its being posited in its exaltation, its own and its friendly signs etc., is termed its positional strength.

interpretation.detailed: Sthana Bala (positional/residential strength) is one of the six Shadbala components. It is calculated by evaluating a planet's dignity — exaltation, Moolatrikona, own sign, friendly sign, neutral, enemy, or debilitation — across each of the six Shadvargas (Rasi/D1, Hora/D2, Drekkana/D3, Navamsa/D9, Dwadasamsa/D12, Trimsamsa/D30). Each varga contributes a proportional Rupa value (per pd-ch04-029). The total across all six vargas forms the Varga-based Sthana Bala. Sthana Bala = aggregate varga dignity across 6 Shadvargas
interpretation.summary: Sthana Bala is the positional strength a planet gains from occupying exaltation, own, or friendly signs across the six Shadvarga charts (D1, D2, D3, D9, D12, D30).

condition.description: Planet's dignity across 6 Shadvargas (D1/D2/D3/D9/D12/D30)

source.original_text: That arising from its being in Kendra and other Bhavas (i.e., Panaphara and Apoklima) will be 1, ½ and ¼ Rupa respectively.

interpretation.detailed: Bhava Bala (house-position strength) is a component of Sthana Bala. A planet's Bhava Bala is determined by which category of house it occupies: Kendra houses (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) give 1 full Rupa; Panaphara houses (2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th) give ½ Rupa; Apoklima houses (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) give ¼ Rupa. See also pd-ch04-030 for the sub-division of values within Kendra houses. Kendra = 1 Rupa; Panaphara = ½ Rupa; Apoklima = ¼ Rupa
interpretation.summary: A planet's Bhava (house position) bala: 1 Rupa in Kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th); ½ Rupa in Panaphara (2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th); ¼ Rupa in Apoklima (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th).

condition.description: Planet in Kendra / Panaphara / Apoklima house

source.original_text: The hermaphrodite planets are strong in the middle, the male ones at the initial and the female ones at the concluding portions of a Rasi.

interpretation.detailed: Each planet is classified by gender, and gains peak sign-positional strength at a specific degree band within any sign: Hermaphrodite planets (Mercury, Saturn) = strongest in the middle 10° (10°–20°); Male planets (Sun, Mars, Jupiter) = strongest at the initial portion (0°–10°); Female planets (Moon, Venus) = strongest at the concluding portion (20°–30°). This is an additional strength modifier within Sthana Bala. Hermaphrodite (Mercury/Saturn) = strongest in middle; Male (Sun/Mars/Jupiter) = strongest at initial; Female (Moon/Venus) = strongest at concluding portion
interpretation.summary: Hermaphrodite planets (Mercury, Saturn) are strongest in the middle of a sign; male planets (Sun, Mars, Jupiter) at the initial portion; female planets (Moon, Venus) at the concluding portion.

condition.description: Planet's gender determines peak strength position within sign

source.original_text: Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, the Moon and the Sun are in their order increasing in their natural strength.

interpretation.detailed: The seven classical planets have a fixed natural (Naisargika) strength order that is independent of chart position. From weakest to strongest: Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Moon, Sun. The Sun is the strongest naturally; Saturn is the weakest. This natural strength order is used as a tiebreaker and baseline factor in Shadbala calculations. Strength order: Saturn < Mars < Mercury < Jupiter < Venus < Moon < Sun
interpretation.summary: The natural inherent strength order of planets from weakest to strongest: Saturn → Mars → Mercury → Jupiter → Venus → Moon → Sun.

condition.description: Inherent natural strength ranking of the seven classical planets

source.original_text: A planet is said to possess strength when he is retrograde or when his rays are full and brilliant, though posited in a depression or inimical Rasi or Amsa.

interpretation.detailed: Retrogression (Vakra gati) is a powerful strength override: a planet in retrograde motion gains strength even if it is simultaneously placed in its sign of debilitation (Neecha) or in an enemy sign or enemy divisional position (Amsa). Similarly, a planet whose rays are full and brilliant — indicating robust radiance — is considered strong despite a debilitated or hostile placement. This rule allows retrograde planets in debilitation to deliver their significations strongly. Planet is strong — delivers strong results despite debilitation or enemy placement
interpretation.summary: A planet in retrograde motion, or with full and brilliant rays, is considered strong regardless of whether it is in its debilitation sign or an enemy sign/Amsa.

condition.description: Planet is retrograde OR has full brilliant rays, even in debilitation or enemy sign/Amsa

source.original_text: Like the Moon, a planet though occupying an exaltation, friendly or his own Rasi or Amsa becomes weak, should his rays be overpowered or eclipsed.

interpretation.detailed: Combustion (Astangata) or eclipse of a planet's rays overrides any positional dignity. Even if a planet is in its exaltation sign, Moolatrikona, own sign, or a friendly sign/divisional position, if its rays are overpowered or eclipsed — primarily by proximity to the Sun causing combustion — it becomes weak and cannot deliver its full or good results. The Moon's eclipse (lunar eclipse) is cited as the archetypal example. This is the eclipse/combustion override rule. Planet is weak — even exaltation/own sign cannot compensate for ray-eclipse
interpretation.summary: A planet whose rays are eclipsed (by Sun's proximity/combustion) or overpowered is weak even if placed in exaltation, own sign, or friendly sign/Amsa.

condition.description: Planet's rays overpowered or eclipsed (combust/eclipsed by Sun)

source.original_text: All planets are strong when they are in their exaltation. The Moon is strong when she has her full Pakshabala and the Sun when he has his full Dig-bala. The other five non-luminous planets are strong when they are retrograde.

interpretation.detailed: Beyond exaltation (which strengthens all planets), each planet has a unique primary strength trigger: the Moon is at its strongest when it has full Pakshabala (i.e., at or near full moon); the Sun is at its strongest when it has full Digbala (i.e., in or near the 10th house/Meridian); the five non-luminous planets (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn) are each at their strongest when in retrograde motion. Moon = strongest at full Pakshabala; Sun = strongest at full Digbala; Mars/Mercury/Jupiter/Venus/Saturn = strongest when retrograde
interpretation.summary: Peak strength: Moon when full Pakshabala; Sun when full Digbala (10th house); five non-luminaries (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn) when retrograde.

condition.description: Planet-specific peak strength conditions

source.original_text: Rahu in Karkataka, Vrishabha, Mesha, Kumbha and Vrischika... is strong.

interpretation.detailed: Rahu (north lunar node) acquires strength when placed in five specific signs: Karkataka (Cancer), Vrishabha (Taurus), Mesha (Aries), Kumbha (Aquarius), and Vrischika (Scorpio). These correspond to signs of exaltation (Cancer per some traditions), own/friendly signs, and signs where Rahu's influence is amplified. This rule applies the planet_category: 'upagraha' for Rahu as per the schema flag resolution. Rahu is strong in these signs
interpretation.summary: Rahu is strong when placed in Karkataka (Cancer), Vrishabha (Taurus), Mesha (Aries), Kumbha (Aquarius), or Vrischika (Scorpio).

source.original_text: Ketu in Meena, Kanya, Vrishabha and the later half of Dhanus... is strong.

interpretation.detailed: Ketu (south lunar node) acquires strength when placed in Meena (Pisces), Kanya (Virgo), Vrishabha (Taurus), or the latter half of Dhanus (Sagittarius, i.e., 15°–30° Sagittarius). These are signs associated with Ketu's exaltation (Scorpio or Sagittarius per various traditions) or natural compatibility. This rule applies the planet_category: 'upagraha' for Ketu. Ketu is strong in these signs
interpretation.summary: Ketu is strong when placed in Meena (Pisces), Kanya (Virgo), Vrishabha (Taurus), or the latter half of Dhanus (Sagittarius).

source.original_text: In Parivesha and Indra-chapa are strong if there be a conjunction of the Moon and the Sun and the time be night.

interpretation.detailed: Parivesha and Indra-chapa are atmospheric phenomena associated with Rahu and Ketu (coronas/halos and rainbows around celestial bodies). When these phenomena occur, the nodes are considered strong under two additional conditions: (1) the Moon and Sun are in conjunction (new moon / Amavasya), AND (2) the birth occurs at night. Both conditions must be simultaneously met for this special strength to apply. Rahu/Ketu are strong
interpretation.summary: When Rahu or Ketu are in Parivesha (halo) or Indra-chapa (rainbow) phenomena, they are strong only if the Moon and Sun are in conjunction AND it is nighttime.

components: Rahu or Ketu in Parivesha or Indra-chapa

source.original_text: If the first Bhava be a biped sign, one Rupa has to be allotted to it; if it be Vrischika, the bala is ¾; if it be any other sign, the strength is ½.

interpretation.detailed: The Lagna's intrinsic sign-based strength (part of Sthana Bala) is assigned as: biped/human signs (Mithuna, Kanya, Tula, first half Dhanus, Kumbha) = 1 full Rupa; Vrischika (Scorpio, the Keeta/reptile sign) = ¾ Rupa; all other signs (watery and quadruped signs: Mesha, Vrishabha, Karkataka, Simha, Makara, Meena, latter half Dhanus) = ½ Rupa. Note: OCR in source text garbles the Vrischika value; ¾ is inferred from standard doctrine. Biped Lagna = 1 Rupa; Vrischika Lagna = ¾ Rupa; other signs = ½ Rupa
interpretation.summary: The inherent strength of the Lagna (Ascendant) varies by sign type: biped/human signs = 1 Rupa; Vrischika = ¾ Rupa; all other signs = ½ Rupa.

condition.description: Sign type of rising Lagna

source.original_text: The strength of the Lagna is equal to that of its lord.

interpretation.detailed: The Lagna's practical operational strength in chart analysis is equated to the strength of its ruling planet (the lord of the rising sign). If the Lagna lord is strong, the Lagna is strong; if the lord is weak, the Lagna is correspondingly weak. This is a foundational principle for assessing the native's overall vitality, health, and life force. Lagna strength = Lagna lord's strength
interpretation.summary: The strength of the Lagna (Ascendant) is equivalent to the strength of its lord.

condition.description: Lagna lord's strength determines Lagna's strength

source.original_text: The Lagna is very powerful when the lord occupies an Upachaya (3rd, 6th, 10th or 11th) house.

interpretation.detailed: When the lord of the Lagna occupies one of the four Upachaya houses (3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th), the Lagna acquires very high strength. Upachaya houses are houses of growth where planets increase in power over time, and a Lagna lord in Upachaya amplifies the Lagna's vitality and positive outcomes for the native. Lagna is very powerful
interpretation.summary: The Lagna becomes very powerful when its lord is placed in an Upachaya house (3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th).

source.original_text: The same is also the case when it is occupied or aspected by its lord, Jupiter or Mercury.

interpretation.detailed: Three beneficial influences can strengthen the Lagna directly: (1) the Lagna lord occupying the Lagna itself (1st house); (2) Jupiter occupying or aspecting the Lagna; (3) Mercury occupying or aspecting the Lagna. Any of these three configurations — as occupant or as aspecting planet — makes the Lagna powerful. Jupiter and Mercury are the most naturally benefic planets and their influence on the Lagna is especially constructive. Lagna is powerful
interpretation.summary: The Lagna is powerful when it is occupied by, or receives the aspect of, its own lord, Jupiter, or Mercury.

condition.description: Lagna occupied OR aspected by: Lagna lord, Jupiter, or Mercury

source.original_text: The same is also the case when it is associated with Venus and is at the same time without the conjunction or aspect of any other planet.

interpretation.detailed: When Venus alone occupies the Lagna — with no other planet in conjunction with Venus in the Lagna, and no other planet aspecting the Lagna — the Lagna acquires strength. The condition of Venus being alone (uncontaminated by other planetary influences) is essential; Venus mixed with malefics or even other benefics does not trigger this rule. Venus alone in Lagna is a specific and exclusive strengthening condition. Lagna is powerful
interpretation.summary: The Lagna becomes powerful when Venus occupies it AND no other planet conjoins or aspects it.

condition.additional: no other planet conjunct or aspecting Lagna

source.original_text: The day-signs possess strength in day-births, while night-signs are declared powerful in night-births.

interpretation.detailed: The classification of signs as diurnal or nocturnal (per Ch01 sloka 8) has a direct strength implication for Lagna and all chart positions: diurnal signs (Simha, Kanya, Tula, Vrischika, Kumbha, Meena) are strong when the native is born during the day; nocturnal signs (Mesha, Vrishabha, Mithuna, Karkataka, Dhanus, Makara) are strong when the native is born at night. This day/night sign strength contributes to Sthana Bala. Day signs strong in day births; night signs strong in night births
interpretation.summary: Diurnal (day) signs gain strength in day-time births; nocturnal (night) signs gain strength in night-time births.

condition.description: Day/night concordance of sign type with birth time

source.original_text: A planet gets one full Rupa as positional strength when he is in his exaltation Rasi. [¾ Rupa in Moolatrikona — OCR garbled]. [½ Rupa in own Rasi — OCR garbled]. When the planet is in a friendly house, his bala is only [¼]. In an inimical house, he gets only very little. The strength is nil when he is in his depression sign or eclipsed by the Sun's rays.

interpretation.detailed: The Sthana Bala (Varga positional strength) per unit of dignity is: Uccha (exaltation sign) = 1 full Rupa (60 Shashtiamsas); Moolatrikona = ¾ Rupa (45 Shashtiamsas); Swa (own sign) = ½ Rupa (30 Shashtiamsas); friendly house = ¼ Rupa (15 Shashtiamsas); inimical/enemy house = very little (exact value not stated, standard = 3.75 Shashtiamsas); depression sign OR eclipsed = nil. These values are per varga and are accumulated across the 6 Shadvargas. Note: fraction values for Moolatrikona and own sign are inferred from standard Shadbala doctrine; OCR in source is garbled for these two lines. Exaltation=1 Rupa; Moolatrikona=¾; own=½; friendly=¼; enemy=tiny; depression/eclipsed=nil
interpretation.summary: Sthana bala by dignity: exaltation=1 Rupa, Moolatrikona=¾, own sign=½, friendly=¼, inimical=very little, debilitation/eclipsed=nil.

condition.description: Planet's dignity level in a varga

source.original_text: The strength of the planets occupying the 4 Kendras has been distinguished: it is ¼ in the 4th house; ½ in the 10th, ¾ in the 7th and full in the 1st or Lagna, thus increasing by ¼ in each stage.

interpretation.detailed: While all Kendra houses give 1 Rupa of Bhava bala in the basic 3-tier system, sloka 8 refines this with a graded scale within the four Kendras themselves: 4th house = ¼ Rupa (weakest Kendra); 10th house = ½ Rupa; 7th house = ¾ Rupa; 1st house (Lagna) = 1 full Rupa (strongest). The progression increases by ¼ Rupa at each step. The Lagna is the most powerful of all four angles for Bhava Bala purposes. 4th = ¼ Rupa; 10th = ½ Rupa; 7th = ¾ Rupa; 1st = 1 Rupa Bhava bala
interpretation.summary: Within the four Kendra houses, Bhava bala values are: 4th house=¼ Rupa, 10th=½, 7th=¾, 1st (Lagna)=1 full Rupa, increasing by ¼ at each stage.

condition.description: Planet in one of the four Kendra houses
