interpretation.summary: When the 1st house is occupied/aspected by benefics and the Lagna lord is in a good house in exaltation/own, Chamara Yoga forms. Native grows daily like waxing Moon, famous, leader, long-lived.

condition.description: 1st house benefically occupied/aspected; 1st lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The person born in the Dhenu Yoga will command good food, drink, etc. He will be wealthy. He will have a very good education all round. He will be blessed with a large family. He will have in plenty gold, gems, wealth, corn, etc., and he will shine like God Kubera.

interpretation.detailed: Dhenu Yoga is the auspicious 2nd-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 2nd house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 2nd lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: commands good food, drink, etc.; wealthy; very good all-round education; blessed with large family; has in plenty gold, gems, wealth, corn; shines like God Kubera. Commands good food; wealthy; well-educated; large family; gold/gems/corn in plenty; shines like Kubera.
interpretation.summary: When the 2nd house is benefically occupied/aspected and its lord is strong, Dhenu Yoga forms. Native commands good food/drink, is wealthy, well-educated, large family, shines like Kubera.

condition.description: 2nd house benefically occupied/aspected; 2nd lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: Praised by his younger brothers who have themselves attained glory, and endowed with valour that commands the admiration of others, the person born in the Saurya Yoga will shine like Sri Rama, fully engrossed in State affairs, fondled/loved by every body and exceedingly famous.

interpretation.detailed: Saurya Yoga is the auspicious 3rd-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 3rd house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 3rd lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: praised by younger brothers (who have themselves attained glory); endowed with valour that commands admiration; shines like Sri Rama; fully engrossed in state affairs; loved by everybody; exceedingly famous. Praised by brothers; valorous; shines like Sri Rama; engrossed in state affairs; exceedingly famous.
interpretation.summary: When the 3rd house is benefically strong, Saurya Yoga forms. Native is praised by younger brothers, valorous, shines like Sri Rama, engrossed in state affairs, loved by everybody, exceedingly famous.

condition.description: 3rd house benefically occupied/aspected; 3rd lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The person born in the Jaladhi or Ambudhi Yoga will be rich in cattle, wealth and corn, will have a beautiful mansion full of relations, an excellent wife, gems, clothes and ornaments. Further, he will hold a respectable and high position. His happiness will be steady and lasting. He will travel on elephants, horses and vehicles. He will be honoured by Kings.

interpretation.detailed: Jaladhi Yoga (also called Ambudhi) is the auspicious 4th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 4th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 4th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: rich in cattle, wealth, and corn; beautiful mansion full of relations; excellent wife; gems, clothes, ornaments; respectable and high position; steady and lasting happiness; travels on elephants, horses, vehicles; honoured by kings; eagerly serves Brahmins and Gods; builds wells and tanks by the roadside. Rich in cattle/wealth/corn; beautiful mansion; excellent wife; gems; high position; steady happiness; honoured by kings.
interpretation.summary: When the 4th house is benefically strong, Jaladhi Yoga forms. Native is rich in cattle/wealth/corn, beautiful mansion, excellent wife, gems, high position, steady happiness, honoured by kings.

condition.description: 4th house benefically occupied/aspected; 4th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The person born in the Chhatra Yoga will be blessed with a happy family life and children. He will be the abode of wealth, renowned, of good speech and learned. He will become a minister to a King. He will be keen-witted and respected by others.

interpretation.detailed: Chhatra Yoga is the auspicious 5th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 5th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 5th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: blessed with happy family life and children; abode of wealth; renowned; good speech; learned; becomes minister to a king; keen-witted; respected by others. Happy family; children; wealth; renowned; minister to a king; keen-witted; respected.
interpretation.summary: When the 5th house is benefically strong, Chhatra Yoga forms. Native has happy family, children, wealth, renown, good speech, learning, becomes minister to a king.

condition.description: 5th house benefically occupied/aspected; 5th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The person who has his birth in the Astra Yoga will forcibly subdue his very powerful foes. He will be rough in his behaviour and arrogant. He will have bruised limbs, but will possess a strong body. He will be quarrelsome.

interpretation.detailed: Astra Yoga is the auspicious 6th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 6th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 6th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: forcibly subdues very powerful foes; rough in behaviour; arrogant; bruised limbs (but) strong body; quarrelsome. Note: this is an auspicious yoga for the 6th house — it boosts combat-related abilities while imparting Martian qualities. Forcibly subdues powerful foes; strong body; rough and arrogant but victorious.
interpretation.summary: When the 6th house is benefically strong, Astra Yoga forms. Native forcibly subdues powerful foes, rough in behaviour, arrogant, bruised limbs but strong body, quarrelsome.

condition.description: 6th house benefically occupied/aspected; 6th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The person born in the Kama Yoga will not even cast a look at others' wives. He will be blessed with an excellent wife, children and relations. With his good qualities, he will shine better than his father, and he will attain to very great prosperity.

interpretation.detailed: Kama Yoga is the auspicious 7th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 7th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 7th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: never casts a look at others' wives; blessed with excellent wife, children, and relations; good qualities shine better than his father; attains very great prosperity. Faithful spouse; excellent wife/children/relations; outshines father; very great prosperity.
interpretation.summary: When the 7th house is benefically strong, Kama Yoga forms. Native is faithful (never looks at others' wives), blessed with excellent wife/children/relations, outshines father, attains very great prosperity.

condition.description: 7th house benefically occupied/aspected; 7th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The man born in the Asura Yoga will spoil others' work and will become a tale-bearer. He will be intent on securing his own interests. He will be poor and have forbidden cravings. He will do mean acts and be troubled by the effects of his own disastrous doings.

interpretation.detailed: Asura Yoga is the auspicious 8th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 8th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 8th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects (paradoxically negative despite benefic classification): spoils others' work; tale-bearer; intent only on own interests; poor; forbidden cravings; does mean acts; troubled by effects of own disastrous doings. This yoga illustrates that even when benefics strengthen the 8th house, the 8th house nature (Dusthana) still dominates the outcome. Spoils others' work; tale-bearer; self-seeking; poor; forbidden cravings; mean acts.
interpretation.summary: When the 8th house is benefically strong, Asura Yoga forms. Despite the auspicious 8th house, native spoils others' work, is a tale-bearer, self-seeking, poor, has forbidden cravings.

condition.description: 8th house benefically occupied/aspected; 8th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: He who has his birth in the Bhagya Yoga will move in a palanquin in the midst full of sounds caused by musical instruments and with chowries waving to and fro. He will have everlasting wealth, will be saluted by eminent men, and will always pursue a righteous course of conduct.

interpretation.detailed: Bhagya Yoga is the auspicious 9th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 9th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 9th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: moves in a palanquin amidst musical instruments with chowries waving; everlasting wealth; saluted by eminent men; always pursues righteous conduct; worships Pitres, Gods, and Brahmins in the most appropriate way; righteous conduct; makes family illustrious; very good heart. Everlasting wealth; saluted by eminent men; righteous conduct; worships Pitres/Gods/Brahmins; illustrious family.
interpretation.summary: When the 9th house is benefically strong, Bhagya Yoga forms. Native moves in palanquin amidst music, everlasting wealth, saluted by eminent men, righteous conduct, worships Pitres/Gods/Brahmins.

condition.description: 9th house benefically occupied/aspected; 9th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The person born in the Khyati Yoga will become a King who will protect his good subjects by following a course of conduct approved by all. He will be blessed with sons, friends, wife and wealth, and will be prosperous and widely renowned.

interpretation.detailed: Khyati Yoga is the auspicious 10th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 10th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 10th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: becomes a king who protects good subjects by a course of conduct approved by all; blessed with sons, friends, wife, and wealth; prosperous; widely renowned. King who protects subjects; sons/friends/wife/wealth; prosperous; widely renowned.
interpretation.summary: When the 10th house is benefically strong, Khyati Yoga forms. Native becomes a king who protects subjects by approved conduct; blessed with sons/friends/wife/wealth; prosperous; widely renowned.

condition.description: 10th house benefically occupied/aspected; 10th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The person born in the Parijata Yoga will always be in the midst of festivities (or auspicious ceremonies), will become a King, will become the lord of much hoarded wealth, will own a large family, will be intent on hearing stories of great people, will be learned and doing something auspicious.

interpretation.detailed: Suparijata Yoga is the auspicious 11th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 11th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 11th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects: always amidst festivities and auspicious ceremonies; becomes a king; lord of much hoarded wealth; owns large family; intent on hearing stories of great people; learned; always doing something auspicious. Always amidst festivities; king; lord of hoarded wealth; large family; learned; auspicious deeds.
interpretation.summary: When the 11th house is benefically strong, Suparijata Yoga forms. Native is always amidst festivities, becomes a king, lord of hoarded wealth, large family, learned, intent on auspicious deeds.

condition.description: 11th house benefically occupied/aspected; 11th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The man born in the Musala Yoga will become the owner of wealth earned with much difficulty; he will suffer humiliation; his wealth will be unsteady; he will spend money only for legitimate purposes. After his demise he will certainly attain heaven; he will be foolish and fickle-minded.

interpretation.detailed: Musala Yoga is the auspicious 12th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 12th house occupied/aspected by benefics AND 12th lord in good house in exaltation/own. Effects (mixed): owns wealth earned with much difficulty; suffers humiliation; unsteady wealth; spends only for legitimate purposes; foolish; fickle-minded. Positive afterlife note: after demise, certainly attains heaven. Wealth earned with difficulty; humiliation; unsteady wealth; spends legitimately; foolish; fickle-minded.
interpretation.summary: When the 12th house is benefically strong, Musala Yoga forms. Native earns wealth with difficulty, suffers humiliation, unsteady wealth, spends legitimately, foolish and fickle-minded — but attains heaven after death.

condition.description: 12th house benefically occupied/aspected; 12th lord in good house/exaltation/own

source.original_text: The man born in an Avayoga will be insignificant. He will suffer from extreme poverty and will be short-lived. He will be humiliated, he will associate with the wicked, will be of bad behaviour and will be deformed. His position itself will be shaky.

interpretation.detailed: Avayoga is the inauspicious 1st-house Bhava yoga. Formation: Lagna lord occupies the 6th, 8th, or 12th house; OR the Lagna is associated with or aspected by malefics. Effects: insignificant; extreme poverty; short-lived; humiliated; associates with the wicked; bad behaviour; deformed; shaky position. Insignificant; extreme poverty; short-lived; humiliated; deformed; shaky position.
interpretation.summary: When the Lagna lord is in the 6th/8th/12th OR the Lagna is occupied/aspected by malefics, Avayoga forms. Native is insignificant, poor, short-lived, humiliated, associates with wicked, deformed.

condition.description: 1st lord in 6/8/12 or Lagna occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: The person born in Nisswa yoga will be devoid of good (kind) words, will have a barren wife, will lie in the midst of bad associates. He will be wanting in intelligence, will have no children, will have no learning, and no power. He will be robbed of his wealth by his enemies.

interpretation.detailed: Nisswayoga is the inauspicious 2nd-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 2nd lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 2nd house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects: devoid of good/kind words; barren wife; bad associates; wanting in intelligence; no children; no learning; no power; robbed of wealth by enemies; bad teeth and eyes. No kind words; barren wife; bad associates; no intelligence/children/learning; wealth robbed by enemies.
interpretation.summary: When the 2nd lord is in 6/8/12 or the 2nd is afflicted by malefics, Nisswayoga forms. Native has no kind words, barren wife, bad associates, no intelligence/children/learning, wealth robbed by enemies.

condition.description: 2nd lord in 6/8/12 or 2nd house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: The person who has his birth in a Mriti Yoga will be vanquished by his enemies, will have no brothers, will be devoid of shame, strength and wealth, overcome by fatigue caused by doing improper acts and will be of an excited temperament.

interpretation.detailed: Mritiyoga is the inauspicious 3rd-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 3rd lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 3rd house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects: vanquished by enemies; no brothers; devoid of shame, strength, and wealth; overcome by fatigue from improper acts; excited temperament. Vanquished by enemies; no brothers; devoid of shame/strength/wealth; fatigued by improper acts.
interpretation.summary: When the 3rd lord is in 6/8/12 or the 3rd is afflicted by malefics, Mritiyoga forms. Native is vanquished by enemies, no brothers, devoid of shame/strength/wealth, fatigued by improper acts, excited temperament.

condition.description: 3rd lord in 6/8/12 or 3rd house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: The man born in a Kuhu Yoga will be bereft of mother, vehicles, friends, happiness, ornaments and relations, will be without a situation or house having lost the one already got, and will be attached to a low female.

interpretation.detailed: Kuhu Yoga is the inauspicious 4th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 4th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 4th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects: bereft of mother, vehicles, friends, happiness, ornaments, and relations; without a situation or house (having lost the one already obtained); attached to a low female. Bereft of mother/vehicles/friends/happiness; homeless; attached to a low female.
interpretation.summary: When the 4th lord is in 6/8/12 or 4th house is afflicted by malefics, Kuhu Yoga forms. Native is bereft of mother/vehicles/friends/happiness, no home, attached to a low female.

condition.description: 4th lord in 6/8/12 or 4th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: He who is born in a Pamara Yoga will have a miserable living and will be indiscriminate. He will be a liar and a cheat. He will lose children or will have no issue at all. He will resort to low and wicked people. He will be an atheist and a glutton.

interpretation.detailed: Pamara Yoga is the inauspicious 5th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 5th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 5th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects: miserable living; indiscriminate; liar and cheat; loses children or has no issue; resorts to low and wicked people; atheist; glutton. Miserable; liar and cheat; no children; resorts to wicked people; atheist; glutton.
interpretation.summary: When the 5th lord is in 6/8/12 or the 5th is afflicted by malefics, Pamara Yoga forms. Native is miserable, indiscriminate, liar, cheat, no children, resorts to low/wicked people, atheist, glutton.

condition.description: 5th lord in 6/8/12 or 5th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: The person born in Harsha Toga will be endowed with happiness, enjoyment, good fortune, and a strong constitution, will overcome his enemies, and will be afraid to commit sinful acts; he will become a friend of illustrious and prominent people. He will have wealth, splendour, friends, fame and sons.

interpretation.detailed: Harsha Yoga is the inauspicious 6th-house Bhava yoga — but produces positive results (Viparita-type). Formation: 6th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 6th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects (positive despite inauspicious category): endowed with happiness, enjoyment, good fortune, and strong constitution; overcomes enemies; afraid to commit sinful acts; friend of illustrious and prominent people; wealth; splendour; friends; fame; sons. The evil of the 6th house cancels itself when afflicted. Happiness; good fortune; strong constitution; overcomes enemies; wealth; fame; sons.
interpretation.summary: When the 6th lord is in 6/8/12 or 6th house is afflicted, Harsha Yoga forms. Despite the inauspicious category, this Viparita-type yoga gives positive results: happiness, strong constitution, overcomes enemies, wealth, fame.

condition.description: 6th lord in 6/8/12 or 6th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: The man born in a Dushkriti Yoga will lose his wife, and be addicted to others' wives, will be roaming on the roads unperceived, will suffer from gonorrhea and such other venereal diseases, and trouble from the sovereign. He will be despised by his relations and suffer distress as a result thereof.

interpretation.detailed: Dushkriti Yoga is the inauspicious 7th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 7th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 7th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects: loses wife; addicted to others' wives; roaming on roads unperceived; suffers from gonorrhoea and venereal diseases; trouble from the sovereign; despised by relations; suffers distress. Loses wife; addicted to others' wives; venereal diseases; trouble from sovereign; despised by relations.
interpretation.summary: When the 7th lord is in 6/8/12 or 7th house is afflicted by malefics, Dushkriti Yoga forms. Native loses wife, addicted to others' wives, venereal diseases, trouble from sovereign, despised by relations.

condition.description: 7th lord in 6/8/12 or 7th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: He who is born in a Sarala Yoga will be long-lived, resolute, fearless, prosperous, and will be endowed with learning, children and riches. He will achieve success in his undertakings, overcome his foes, be pure and widely celebrated.

interpretation.detailed: Sarala Yoga is the inauspicious 8th-house Bhava yoga — but produces positive results (Viparita-type). Formation: 8th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 8th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects (positive): long-lived; resolute; fearless; prosperous; endowed with learning, children, and riches; achieves success in undertakings; overcomes foes; pure; widely celebrated. The evil of the 8th (longevity hazard) cancels itself when the 8th lord occupies another Dusthana. Long-lived; resolute; fearless; prosperous; learning/children/riches; overcomes foes; pure; celebrated.
interpretation.summary: When the 8th lord is in 6/8/12 or 8th house is afflicted, Sarala Yoga forms. Viparita-type: long-lived, resolute, fearless, prosperous, learning, children, riches, overcomes foes, pure, celebrated.

condition.description: 8th lord in 6/8/12 or 8th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: The person born in Nirbhagya Yoga will lose all his paternal property such as lands, house, etc. he will despise the good and elders and will be irreligious. He will wear old and worn-out clothes, will be indigent and reduced to great misery.

interpretation.detailed: Nirbhagya Yoga is the inauspicious 9th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 9th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 9th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects: loses all paternal property (lands, house, etc.); despises good and elders; irreligious; wears old and worn-out clothes; indigent; reduced to great misery. Loses paternal property; despises good and elders; irreligious; indigent; great misery.
interpretation.summary: When the 9th lord is in 6/8/12 or 9th house is afflicted, Nirbhagya Yoga forms. Native loses paternal property, despises good and elders, irreligious, wears old clothes, indigent, great misery.

condition.description: 9th lord in 6/8/12 or 9th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: The effect of a person's birth in Duryoga will be that anything done by his own bodily labour becomes fruitless. He will be insignificant in the eyes of the public. He will be a traitor to the people, will be highly selfish, and caring to feed his own belly. He will be constantly absent from home and living abroad.

interpretation.detailed: Duryoga is the inauspicious 10th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 10th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 10th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects: anything done by bodily labour becomes fruitless; insignificant in the eyes of the public; traitor to the people; highly selfish; cares only to feed own belly; constantly absent from home; living abroad. Work fruitless; insignificant in public; traitor; selfish; lives abroad.
interpretation.summary: When the 10th lord is in 6/8/12 or 10th house is afflicted, Duryoga forms. Native's work is fruitless, insignificant in public, traitor, selfish, lives abroad, constantly absent from home.

condition.description: 10th lord in 6/8/12 or 10th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: He who is born in Daridra Yoga will be loaded with debts, cruel, foremost among the poor, will suffer from ear-troubles, will be devoid of good brotherhood, will entangle himself in criminal or sinful actions, will speak indecently and will be a menial to others.

interpretation.detailed: Daridra Yoga is the inauspicious 11th-house Bhava yoga. Formation: 11th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 11th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects: loaded with debts; cruel; foremost among the poor; ear troubles; devoid of good brotherhood; entangles in criminal/sinful actions; speaks indecently; menial to others. Loaded with debts; poor; ear troubles; no good brotherhood; criminal actions; speaks indecently; menial.
interpretation.summary: When the 11th lord is in 6/8/12 or 11th house is afflicted, Daridra Yoga forms. Native is loaded with debts, poor, ear troubles, no good brotherhood, criminal actions, speaks indecently, serves as a menial.

condition.description: 11th lord in 6/8/12 or 11th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: The person born in a Vimala Yoga will spend little and save much money. He will be good to everybody. He will be happy and independent and will have a respectable profession or conduct and be renowned for his good qualities.

interpretation.detailed: Vimala Yoga is the inauspicious 12th-house Bhava yoga — but produces positive results (Viparita-type). Formation: 12th lord in 6th/8th/12th OR 12th house associated/aspected by malefics. Effects (positive): spends little and saves much money; good to everybody; happy and independent; respectable profession or conduct; renowned for good qualities. The evil of the 12th (expenditure/loss) cancels itself when afflicted. Spends little; saves much; good to everybody; happy and independent; respectable profession; renowned for good qualities.
interpretation.summary: When the 12th lord is in 6/8/12 or 12th house is afflicted, Vimala Yoga forms. Viparita-type: spends little, saves much, good to everybody, happy, independent, respectable profession, renowned for good qualities.

condition.description: 12th lord in 6/8/12 or 12th house occupied/aspected by malefics

source.original_text: If the lords of the 8th, 6th and 12th houses occupying in strength Kendra or Trikona houses, and the lords of the 1st, 10th, 4th and 9th houses be weak or eclipsed and be posited in the 6th, 8th and 12th houses, the result is a bad yoga (Kuryoga).

interpretation.detailed: Strength polarity rule (negative condition): If the lords of the 8th, 6th, and 12th houses are strong AND occupy Kendra or Trikona houses, while simultaneously the lords of the 1st, 10th, 4th, and 9th houses are weak or eclipsed AND are posited in the 6th, 8th, or 12th houses — the result is an evil yoga (called Kuryoga). The Dusthana lords overpower the auspicious lords in this configuration. Evil yoga — Dusthana lords dominate; auspicious house lords are overwhelmed; bad results overall.
interpretation.summary: When the 6th/8th/12th lords are strong and in Kendra/Trikona, AND the 1st/4th/9th/10th lords are weak/eclipsed in Dusthana houses, the result is an evil yoga (Kuryoga).

condition.description: 6th/8th/12th lords strong in Kendra/Trikona; 1st/4th/9th/10th lords weak/eclipsed in 6/8/12

source.original_text: But if the above position be reversed, i.e., the lords of the 8th, 6th and 12th being weak or eclipsed occupy those houses, and the lords of the 1st, 4th, 9th and 10th houses being strong occupy Kendra or Kona houses, the person concerned will be a King, fortunate, wealthy, happy and virtuously disposed.

interpretation.detailed: Strength polarity rule (positive condition — reverse of pd-ch06-081): If the lords of the 8th, 6th, and 12th houses are weak or eclipsed AND occupy those very Dusthana houses, while simultaneously the lords of the 1st, 4th, 9th, and 10th houses are strong AND occupy Kendra or Trikona houses — the person is a King: fortunate, wealthy, happy, and virtuously disposed. The auspicious lords dominate completely while Dusthana lords are confined and weakened. King — fortunate, wealthy, happy, and virtuously disposed.
interpretation.summary: When the 1st/4th/9th/10th lords are strong in Kendra or Trikona, AND the 6th/8th/12th lords are weak/eclipsed in their own Dusthana houses — the native is a King, fortunate, wealthy, happy, virtuous.

condition.description: 1st/4th/9th/10th lords strong in Kendra/Trikona; 6th/8th/12th lords weak/eclipsed in their own Dusthana houses

source.original_text: When three or more planets are posited in Kendras in their signs of exaltation or own signs, the person concerned will be a widely renowned king.

interpretation.detailed: If three or more planets are posited in Kendra houses (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) each in its own sign or sign of exaltation, the native will be a widely renowned king. The qualifying threshold is 3 planets; the elevated threshold of 5+ is separately encoded in pd-ch07-002. All seven classical planets are eligible; the planets must be in their own specific Kendra placements. Widely renowned king
interpretation.summary: When 3 or more planets occupy Kendra houses in their own sign or sign of exaltation, the native becomes a widely renowned king.

condition.description: 3 or more planets in Kendra (1/4/7/10) each in own sign or exaltation sign

source.original_text: If five or more planets are so placed, even a person born in an ordinary family becomes a ruler of the world possessed of elephants and horses.

interpretation.detailed: When five or more planets are posited in Kendra houses each in its own sign or exaltation, even a native born into an ordinary (non-royal) family will become a ruler of the world, possessing elephants and horses. This represents an escalation of the 3-planet threshold in pd-ch07-001. The emphasis on 'even an ordinary family' underlines that this yoga overrides birth circumstances entirely at the 5+ threshold. Ruler of the world even if born in ordinary family
interpretation.summary: When 5 or more planets occupy Kendra houses in own/exaltation sign, even a person of ordinary birth becomes ruler of the world.

condition.description: 5 or more planets in Kendra (1/4/7/10) each in own sign or exaltation sign

source.original_text: If a person belonging to a royal family is not under any evil yoga, nor eclipsed, he will be a king.

interpretation.detailed: If the native belongs to a royal family and their chart is free from any evil yoga (malefic combinations) and the Moon or other relevant planets are not eclipsed (combust or otherwise weakened), the native will be a king. This rule operates primarily on birth circumstances (royal family) combined with the absence of weakening yogas. It implies that royal potential is suppressed only by evil yogas or eclipse conditions. King
interpretation.summary: A native of royal lineage who is neither under an evil yoga nor eclipsed at birth will be a king.

condition.description: Royal family birth + no evil yoga + no planet eclipsed/combust

source.original_text: If three or more planets are placed in Kendras in their own signs or signs of exaltation, royals will be kings and others will be their equals.

interpretation.detailed: If three or more planets are placed in Kendra houses in their own signs or signs of exaltation, the result is differentiated by birth: those born in royal families become kings, and those born in non-royal families attain a status equal to kings. This rule is a reformulation of Sloka 1 (pd-ch07-001) with an explicit birth-class differentiation. Note that Sloka 2 also introduces the eclipse-free royal yoga (pd-ch07-003) in its first half. Royals become kings; non-royals become equal to kings
interpretation.summary: When 3+ planets are in Kendra in own/exaltation signs, those of royal birth become kings; others become their equals.

condition.description: 3 or more planets in Kendra in own sign or exaltation

source.original_text: If there is a single retrograde and brilliant planet posited in its sign of depression in a good house, the person becomes the equal of a king.

interpretation.detailed: When exactly one planet is simultaneously retrograde, brilliant (strong in luminosity/speed), and placed in its sign of depression, and this planet occupies a good house (typically a Kendra or Trikona), the native becomes equal in status to a king. The retrograde motion here acts as a Neechabhanga mechanism — a depressed retrograde planet gains strength and reversal of its debility. This is the lowest tier of a three-level retrograde-debilitation yoga (see pd-ch07-006 and pd-ch07-007 for 2-3 and many-planet variants). Equal of a king
interpretation.summary: A single planet that is retrograde, brilliant, and in depression yet in a good house elevates the native to the equal of a king.

condition.description: Exactly 1 planet that is retrograde + brilliant + in own sign of depression + in a good house (Kendra/Trikona)

source.original_text: If there are two or three such planets, he becomes a king.

interpretation.detailed: When two or three planets simultaneously satisfy the conditions of being retrograde, brilliant, and in their sign of depression, each placed in a good house, the native attains the status of a king. This is the middle tier of the three-level retrograde-debilitation yoga (see pd-ch07-005 for the 1-planet tier and pd-ch07-007 for the many-planet tier). The retrograde motion is understood to cancel or reverse the debilitation, producing a Neechabhanga-type elevation. King
interpretation.summary: When 2 or 3 planets are retrograde, brilliant, and in depression in good houses, the native becomes a king.

condition.description: 2 or 3 planets each retrograde + brilliant + in depression + in good house

source.original_text: If there are many, he will become a king with all insignia — crown, umbrella, and chowries.

interpretation.detailed: When many planets (typically 4 or more) are simultaneously retrograde, brilliant, and in their signs of depression, each placed in a good house, the native becomes a king bearing all royal insignia: crown, umbrella (chatra), and chowries (chamara). This is the highest tier of the three-level retrograde-debilitation yoga. The enumeration of specific insignia (crown, umbrella, chowries) is a conventional Vedic indicator of the highest kingly authority. King with full royal insignia (crown, umbrella, chowries)
interpretation.summary: Many planets retrograde, brilliant, and in depression in good houses → king with crown, umbrella, and chowries (full royal insignia).

condition.description: Many (4+) planets each retrograde + brilliant + in depression + in good house

source.original_text: If two or more planets have Digbala and the person belongs to a royal family, he will be a king.

interpretation.detailed: When two or more planets occupy their houses of directional strength (Digbala — Sun/Mars in 10th, Moon/Venus in 4th, Mercury/Jupiter in 1st, Saturn in 7th) and the native is born into a royal family, the native will be a king. Digbala assignments are defined in the Shadbala chapter (Ch04). This rule requires both the planetary condition and the birth condition. Compare with pd-ch07-009 which removes the royal-family requirement at the 5-planet threshold. King
interpretation.summary: Two or more planets with directional strength (Digbala), combined with royal birth, produces a king.

condition.description: 2 or more planets with Digbala (in their directional strength houses) + royal family birth

source.original_text: If five planets (excluding Saturn) have Digbala, or four of them have Digbala, even one born in an ordinary family will be a king.

interpretation.detailed: When five planets (excluding Saturn) have Digbala, or when four planets (the text implies any four, including or excluding Saturn) have Digbala, even a native of ordinary birth will become a king. The exclusion of Saturn in the 5-planet count is notable — Saturn's Digbala in the 7th house is considered less potent for kingship purposes, or the five-planet threshold must be met by the remaining six non-Saturn planets. The 4-planet alternative removes the Saturn exclusion qualifier. This rule overrides birth conditions entirely at the high Digbala threshold. Even ordinary-born becomes king
interpretation.summary: Five planets excluding Saturn (or four planets) with Digbala make even an ordinary-born native a king.

condition.description: 5 non-Saturn planets with Digbala OR 4 planets with Digbala; birth condition not required

source.original_text: If the Lagna is in Vargottama Navamsa or if the Moon is in Vargottama Navamsa and four planets aspect the Lagna, even a person born in a low family will become a king.

interpretation.detailed: This rule has two alternative formations: (1) If the Lagna itself is in Vargottama Navamsa (same sign in both Rasi and Navamsa charts), the native born even in a low family will become a king. (2) Alternatively, if the Moon is in Vargottama Navamsa and four planets aspect the Lagna, the same outcome applies. Vargottama is considered a position of exceptional strength in the divisional chart system. The four-planet Lagna aspect in the second condition provides the additional activation needed when only the Moon is Vargottama. Even low-born becomes king
interpretation.summary: Vargottama Navamsa Lagna, or Moon in Vargottama Navamsa with four planets aspecting Lagna, elevates even a low-born native to kingship.

condition.description: Lagna in Vargottama Navamsa OR (Moon in Vargottama Navamsa AND 4 planets aspect Lagna)

source.original_text: If the lord of the Lagna and the lord of the 9th house are both in their Vargottama Navamsa and are placed in a Kendra or the 9th house, the person will be a king who rides a golden vehicle and an elephant.

interpretation.detailed: When the lord of the Lagna (Ascendant) and the lord of the 9th house are each in their Vargottama Navamsa (same sign in Rasi and Navamsa) AND each is placed in a Kendra (1/4/7/10) or the 9th house, the native will be a king who rides a golden vehicle and an elephant. The conjunction of the Lagna lord (self/body) and the 9th lord (fortune/dharma) both in Vargottama is a doubly powerful formation. Their placement in Kendra/9th — the strongest houses — amplifies the yoga's potency. King who rides a golden vehicle and elephant
interpretation.summary: Both the Lagna lord and 9th lord in Vargottama Navamsa, placed in a Kendra or 9th house, produce a king who rides a golden vehicle and elephant.

condition.description: Lagna lord in Vargottama Navamsa in Kendra or 9th AND 9th lord in Vargottama Navamsa in Kendra or 9th

source.original_text: If the full Moon is aspected by a planet in its sign of exaltation or own sign, even a person born in a low family will be a king.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is full (at or near Purnima — typically 12th to 15th tithi) and receives the aspect of any planet placed in its sign of exaltation or own sign, even a native born in a low-ranking family will become a king. The full Moon's inherent strength (Paksha Bala maximum) combined with the strengthening aspect of an exalted/own-sign planet creates a powerful yoga. The 'low family' caveat emphasises that birth circumstances are transcended. Even low-born becomes king
interpretation.summary: A full Moon receiving the aspect of a planet in exaltation or own sign elevates even a low-born native to kingship.

condition.description: Moon at full (Purnima) aspected by a planet in exaltation or own sign

source.original_text: If the full Moon is in a Kendra other than the Lagna, the person will be a king possessed of elephants and horses.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is full and occupies a Kendra house other than the Lagna (i.e., the 4th, 7th, or 10th house), the native will be a king who possesses elephants and horses. The exclusion of the Lagna suggests that Lagna placement, while powerful, is here treated separately — the rule specifically benefits from the Moon's angular placement away from the Ascendant. The possession of elephants and horses is a traditional Vedic marker of great wealth and military power. King possessed of elephants and horses
interpretation.summary: A full Moon in a Kendra other than the Lagna (i.e., 4th, 7th, or 10th) produces a king with elephants and horses.

source.original_text: If Venus is in Aswini Nakshatra and is in the Lagna and is aspected by three or more planets, the person will be a king who destroys his enemies.

interpretation.detailed: When Venus occupies Aswini Nakshatra (0°–13°20' Mesha) and is placed in the Lagna (1st house), AND three or more planets aspect this Venus, the native will be a king who destroys his enemies. Aswini is the first nakshatra, ruled by Ketu/Ashwini Kumaras — its energy is swift, healing, and initiating. Venus in Aswini combines Venusian charm and resources with Aswini's martial initiative. The requirement of 3+ planet aspects creates a concentration of planetary energy on the Lagna, amplifying the yoga. King who destroys his enemies
interpretation.summary: Venus in Aswini Nakshatra occupying the Lagna and receiving aspects from three or more planets produces a king who destroys enemies.

condition.description: Venus in Aswini Nakshatra in Lagna (1st house) aspected by 3 or more planets

source.original_text: If the lord of the Lagna is strong, placed in the 2nd house (not in depression or enemy's sign) and is in conjunction with Venus, the person will be a king.

interpretation.detailed: When the lord of the Lagna is strong, placed in the 2nd house (not in debilitation and not in an enemy's sign), and is in conjunction with Venus, the native will be a king. The 2nd house governs wealth, family, and speech — the Lagna lord here is deposited in the house of resources while conjunct the planet of luxury and beauty (Venus). The negation conditions (not in depression, not in enemy sign) are important — a weakened Lagna lord would not activate the yoga even with the other conditions met. King
interpretation.summary: A strong Lagna lord placed in the 2nd house (not in depression or enemy sign) and conjunct Venus produces a king.

condition.description: Lagna lord strong in 2nd house (not in debilitation, not in enemy sign) + conjunct Venus

source.original_text: If Mars is in Mesha, Simha or Dhanus as Lagna and is aspected by friendly planets, the person will be the king of the earth.

interpretation.detailed: When Mars occupies the Lagna (1st house) and that Lagna is one of the three fire signs — Mesha (Aries), Simha (Leo), or Dhanus (Sagittarius) — and Mars receives aspects from friendly planets, the native will be the king of the earth. Mars is particularly strong in fire signs: Mesha is its own sign (Moolatrikona 0°–12°), Simha is friendly, and Dhanus is friendly. The three fire signs are natural houses for Martian energy. Friendly aspects reinforce Mars's strength and positivity. King of the earth
interpretation.summary: Mars placed in a fire-sign Lagna (Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius) and aspected by friendly planets makes the native king of the earth.

condition.description: Mars in Lagna (1st house) in a fire sign (Mesha/Simha/Dhanus) + aspected by friendly planets

source.original_text: If the lord of the 10th house is in the 9th and the lord of the 9th is in the 10th house, the person will be a king extolled by the people.

interpretation.detailed: When the lord of the 10th house is placed in the 9th house, and the lord of the 9th house is placed in the 10th house (mutual exchange / Parivartana yoga between the two most powerful Kendra and Trikona lords), the native becomes a king extolled by the people. The 9th lord (dharma, fortune, father) and 10th lord (karma, kingship, action) exchanging signs creates an exceptionally powerful Dharma-Karma Adhipati Parivartana. This is a variety of Maha Parivartana yoga (pd-ch06-043 range) applied specifically to the 9th and 10th lords. King extolled by the people
interpretation.summary: Mutual exchange (Parivartana) of the 9th and 10th house lords produces a king praised and extolled by his people.

condition.description: 10th lord in 9th house AND 9th lord in 10th house (mutual exchange)

source.original_text: If the Sun and the Moon are at the centre of Dhanus, Saturn is in the Lagna (which is Dhanus or Meena or Tula), and Mars is in its sign of exaltation, the person will be a mighty king feared by his enemies.

interpretation.detailed: This sloka describes a highly specific astronomical configuration: the Sun and Moon both placed in the central degrees of Dhanus (Sagittarius), Saturn in the Lagna (which must be Dhanus, Meena, or Tula — the three signs where Saturn has dignity: own/exaltation/moolatrikona), and Mars in its sign of exaltation (Makara — Capricorn). The native will be a mighty king feared by enemies. The specificity of this yoga (particular signs, mid-sign placement, exact three-way configuration) makes it a rare but precise predictor. The Lagna options are parenthetical: Saturn in Lagna requires Dhanus (Saturn's Moolatrikona), Meena (Saturn neutral but strong), or Tula (Saturn's exaltation) as the Lagna. Mighty king feared by enemies
interpretation.summary: Sun and Moon at the centre of Sagittarius, Saturn in Lagna (Dhanus/Meena/Tula), and Mars in exaltation produce a mighty king feared by his enemies.

condition.description: Sun + Moon in central Dhanus + Saturn in Lagna (Dhanus/Meena/Tula) + Mars in exaltation (Makara)

source.original_text: If the full Moon is in the Navamsa of the Sun and benefics (unassociated with malefics) are placed in the Kendras, the person will be a king possessed of many elephants.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is full and is in the Navamsa of the Sun (i.e., in Simha Navamsa — the Navamsa position corresponding to the Sun's own sign Leo), and benefic planets (Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, waxing Moon) are placed in the Kendra houses (1/4/7/10) without association with malefics, the native will be a king who possesses many elephants. The Sun's Navamsa (Simha) represents solar authority; the full Moon there combines lunar completeness with solar power. The requirement that benefics be unassociated with malefics is a purity condition. King possessed of many elephants
interpretation.summary: A full Moon in the Sun's Navamsa (Simha Navamsa) combined with benefics unafflicted by malefics in Kendra houses produces a king with many elephants.

condition.description: Full Moon in Sun's Navamsa (Simha Navamsa) + benefics in Kendra unassociated with malefics

source.original_text: If the full Moon is aspected by three strong planets placed in their own Amsas and aspected by benefics, the person will be a king who vanquishes his enemies.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is full and three strong planets (each placed in their own Amsa/divisional position) aspect the Moon, and these aspecting planets are additionally aspected by benefics, the native will be a king who vanquishes enemies. The triple requirement — full Moon, strong own-Amsa planets aspecting it, and those planets themselves receiving benefic aspects — creates a deeply layered yoga. 'Own Amsa' refers to a planet placed in a divisional chart sign it owns, adding an extra layer of strength beyond basic Rasi placement. King who vanquishes enemies
interpretation.summary: Full Moon receiving aspects from three strong planets in their own Amsas (further aspected by benefics) produces a king who vanquishes enemies.

condition.description: Full Moon aspected by 3 strong planets in own Amsas, those planets aspected by benefics

source.original_text: If the Moon is in its Vargottama Navamsa and is aspected by a strong planet, and there is no malefic planet in the Lagna, the person will be an emperor with a beautiful body.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is in Vargottama Navamsa (same sign in both Rasi and Navamsa), receives the aspect of a strong planet, and no malefic planet occupies the Lagna, the native will be an emperor with a beautiful body. The Vargottama Moon is exceptionally strong; the strong planet's aspect reinforces it; the clean Lagna (free of malefic influence) ensures the physical body and self are also untainted. The dual result — emperor-level status plus physical beauty — is characteristic of the Vargottama Moon's combination of strength and grace. Emperor with a beautiful body
interpretation.summary: Moon in Vargottama Navamsa, aspected by a strong planet, with no malefic in the Lagna, produces an emperor with a beautiful body.

condition.description: Moon in Vargottama Navamsa + aspected by strong planet + no malefic in Lagna

source.original_text: If Jupiter, Mercury, Venus or the Moon is in the 9th house, strong, uneclipsed, and aspected by or associated with a friendly planet, the person will be a great king worshipped like a deity.

interpretation.detailed: When any of the four great benefics (Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, or Moon) is placed in the 9th house, is strong (in dignity or by Shadbala), is not eclipsed (not combust or otherwise weakened), and receives the aspect of or is associated with a friendly planet, the native will be a great king worshipped like a deity. The 9th house governs dharma, fortune, and divine grace. A benefic in the 9th, unspoiled by eclipse and reinforced by friendly planets, activates the highest divine-grace mechanism. The 'worshipped like a deity' qualifier places this yoga above ordinary kingship. Great king worshipped like a deity
interpretation.summary: Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, or Moon in the 9th house — strong, uneclipsed, with friendly planet aspect or association — produces a great king worshipped like a deity.

source.original_text: If Venus, Jupiter and Saturn are in Meena, the Moon is nearly full and in its sign of exaltation, the Sun is aspected by Mars, and Mesha is the rising sign, the person will be a king with a vast army raising clouds of dust.

interpretation.detailed: This sloka describes an astronomically specific formation: Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn all three in Meena (Pisces); the Moon nearly full and in Vrishabha (its sign of exaltation, 3°); the Sun receiving the aspect of Mars; and Mesha (Aries) as the Lagna. The native born under this configuration will be a king with a vast army raising clouds of dust — a vivid martial image indicating a mighty military force on the move. This yoga requires exact simultaneous positioning of six planets, making it extremely rare. The specificity of Meena as a triple-planet congregation is notable. King with a vast army raising clouds of dust
interpretation.summary: Venus, Jupiter, and Saturn all in Meena; Moon nearly full in exaltation (Vrishabha); Sun aspected by Mars; Mesha Lagna — produces a king with a vast army raising dust clouds.

condition.description: Venus + Jupiter + Saturn in Meena AND Moon nearly full in Vrishabha (exaltation) AND Sun aspected by Mars AND Lagna = Mesha

source.original_text: If a person is born at night, and benefics are in depression or inimical signs in the 11th, 6th or 3rd house, or if they are at the highest point of exaltation, or if all of them are in Kendras with bright rays, and the Moon is in Cancer or the 10th house, the person will be an emperor ruling the three worlds.

interpretation.detailed: When the native is born at night, AND one of three benefic conditions applies — (a) benefics in depression or inimical signs placed in the 11th, 6th, or 3rd houses, OR (b) benefics at their highest exaltation point, OR (c) all benefics in Kendra houses with bright rays — AND the Moon is in Cancer (its own sign) or in the 10th house, the native will be an emperor ruling the three worlds. The night-birth condition is significant: benefics in depression/inimical signs in the Upachaya houses (11th, 6th, 3rd) are considered compensated by night-time birth (when Moon, Venus, and Saturn gain Kala Bala / temporal strength). This is a polarity-reversal yoga for debilitated benefics in supportive houses. Emperor ruling the three worlds
interpretation.summary: Night birth with specific benefic placement conditions and Moon in Cancer or 10th house produces an emperor ruling the three worlds.

condition.description: Night birth + (benefics in bad signs in 11/6/3 OR highest exaltation OR all benefics in Kendra with bright rays) + Moon in Cancer or 10th

source.original_text: If the full Moon is in its Vargottama Navamsa, the person will become a mighty ruler with immense fame and many horses.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is full and occupies its Vargottama Navamsa position (the Moon's sign in the Rasi chart is the same as in the Navamsa chart), the native will become a mighty ruler with immense fame and many horses. This is a concise single-condition yoga combining two Moon strengths: maximum Paksha Bala (full Moon) and maximum divisional dignity (Vargottama). The immense fame and many horses are signature markers of a powerful sovereign in classical Vedic literature. Mighty ruler with immense fame and many horses
interpretation.summary: A full Moon in Vargottama Navamsa (same sign in Rasi and Navamsa) produces a mighty ruler with immense fame and many horses.

condition.description: Moon full (Purnima) in Vargottama Navamsa

source.original_text: If Jupiter and the Moon are in a Kendra and are aspected by Venus, and no planet is in its sign of depression, the person will be a king with unparalleled fame.

interpretation.detailed: When Jupiter and the Moon are both placed in a Kendra house (1/4/7/10) and receive the aspect of Venus, AND no planet in the entire chart is in its sign of depression, the native will be a king with unparalleled fame. The three great natural benefics (Jupiter, Moon, Venus) are all activated here — Jupiter and Moon together in Kendra, with Venus aspecting them. The absence of any debilitated planet in the chart is a purity condition that ensures no negative yogas counteract the positive formations. This is a triple-benefic activation yoga. King with unparalleled fame
interpretation.summary: Jupiter and Moon together in a Kendra, aspected by Venus, with no planet in debilitation, produces a king with unparalleled fame.

condition.description: Jupiter + Moon in Kendra + aspected by Venus + no planet in debilitation in chart

source.original_text: If the Moon is in a water sign or in a water Amsa equal to the Lagna or in its own or benefic Varga, the person will be a king who does good to his subjects and possesses many elephants.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is in a water sign (Karka, Vrishchika, or Meena) or in a water Amsa (divisional position) that is equal to (matches) the Lagna, or when the Moon is in its own Varga or a benefic Varga, the native will be a king who does good to his subjects and possesses many elephants. The water sign association of the Moon activates its nurturing, emotional, and caring qualities — hence the emphasis on 'doing good to subjects.' The elephant possession signals wealth and military power. This is the positive variant of the Sloka 19 Moon yoga (compare pd-ch07-028 for the negative variant when Moon is not in Kendra). King who does good to subjects, possesses many elephants
interpretation.summary: Moon in a water sign or water Amsa matching the Lagna, or in own/benefic Varga, produces a benevolent king with many elephants.

condition.description: Moon in water sign OR water Amsa equal to Lagna OR Moon in own/benefic Varga

source.original_text: If such a Moon is not in a Kendra and there are no malefics in Kendras, the person will be a king with elephants but one who oppresses his people.

interpretation.detailed: This is the shadow variant of pd-ch07-027: when the Moon satisfies the same water sign/benefic Varga condition but is NOT placed in a Kendra house, AND no malefics are in Kendra houses, the native will be a king who possesses elephants but oppresses his people. The absence from Kendra weakens the Moon's beneficial expression — the wealth (elephants) manifests, but the virtuous nature does not. The absence of malefics in Kendras is an additional qualifier: if malefics were in Kendras, a different (worse) outcome might apply. This rule illustrates that the same planetary quality can produce materially similar but morally opposite results depending on house position. King with elephants but oppresses his people
interpretation.summary: When the same water/benefic-Varga Moon (from pd-ch07-027) is not in a Kendra, and no malefics are in Kendras, the native is a king with elephants but an oppressive ruler.

condition.description: Moon in water sign or benefic Varga (same as pd-ch07-027) BUT not in Kendra + no malefics in Kendra

source.original_text: If Venus is aspected by Jupiter and the person belongs to a royal family, he will be a king.

interpretation.detailed: When Venus receives the aspect of Jupiter and the native is born into a royal family, the native will be a king. The Jupiter-Venus aspect is a classic benefic reinforcement — Jupiter's dharmic aspect (5th, 7th, 9th) falling on Venus activates Venusian wealth, pleasure, and kingly comfort in a dharmic context. The royal family birth is a co-requisite that activates the latent royalty in the chart. King
interpretation.summary: Venus receiving Jupiter's aspect, combined with royal family birth, produces a king.

condition.description: Venus aspected by Jupiter + royal family birth

source.original_text: If Jupiter is in the Lagna (except Makara), the person will be a king with rut elephants.

interpretation.detailed: When Jupiter occupies the Lagna (1st house / Ascendant) in any sign except Makara (Capricorn), the native will be a king with rut elephants (elephants in musth — the sign of the most powerful battle elephants). The exclusion of Makara is significant: Jupiter is debilitated in Capricorn and loses its Lagna-strengthening quality there. In all other signs, Jupiter in the Lagna activates its full benefic power over the self, body, and overall destiny. Rut elephants (elephants in musth) represent the highest military and kingly power — only the most powerful kings commanded them. King with rut elephants
interpretation.summary: Jupiter in the Lagna in any sign except Makara (Capricorn, where it is debilitated) produces a king with rut elephants.

condition.note: Valid for all Lagnas except Makara (Jupiter debilitated)

source.original_text: If the lord of the Lagna is in a Kendra with full strength, the person will be a ruler of men.

interpretation.detailed: When the lord of the Lagna is placed in a Kendra house (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th) and possesses full strength (high Shadbala or placed in dignity — own sign, exaltation, or Moolatrikona), the native will be a ruler of men. This is a clean, powerful single-condition yoga: the self-indicator (Lagna lord) in its strongest angular position. 'Full strength' implies the Lagna lord is not merely placed in a Kendra but is also dignified — not in depression, not combust, not in enemy sign. Ruler of men
interpretation.summary: The Lagna lord placed in a Kendra house at full strength makes the native a ruler of men.

source.original_text: If Mercury is in a Kendra and is aspected by Jupiter, the orders of the person will be obeyed by kings.

interpretation.detailed: When Mercury is placed in a Kendra house and receives the aspect of Jupiter, the native's orders will be obeyed by kings — making the native, in effect, more powerful than kings or a supreme advisor/minister who commands royalty. Mercury governs intellect, speech, communication, and administration; Jupiter bestows wisdom and authority. Their combination in a Kendra creates a formidable administrative-intelligence yoga. The result ('orders obeyed by kings') may indicate the native is a great statesman, advisor, or sovereign whose commands even royals follow. Orders obeyed by kings
interpretation.summary: Mercury placed in a Kendra and aspected by Jupiter produces a person whose orders are obeyed by kings.

source.original_text: If a planet is at the highest point of exaltation and is aspected by a friendly planet, the person will be a king.

interpretation.detailed: When any planet is at the highest point of its exaltation (paramauchcha — the exact exaltation degree: Sun 10° Mesha, Moon 3° Vrishabha, Mars 28° Makara, Mercury 15° Kanya, Jupiter 5° Karka, Venus 27° Meena, Saturn 20° Tula) and receives the aspect of a friendly planet, the native will be a king. Paramauchcha is the strongest possible planetary position — the planet is at peak dignity. The friendly aspect confirms and activates this strength rather than allowing it to remain latent. King
interpretation.summary: Any planet at its exact degree of highest exaltation (paramauchcha), aspected by a friendly planet, produces a king.

condition.description: Any planet at paramauchcha (exact exaltation degree) + aspected by friendly planet

source.original_text: If it is also associated with a friendly planet, the person will be immensely wealthy.

interpretation.detailed: This is the escalation of pd-ch07-033: when the paramauchcha planet is not only aspected by a friendly planet but is also in conjunction (association) with a friendly planet, the result escalates from 'king' to 'immensely wealthy.' The double friendly reinforcement — both aspect and conjunction — maximises the paramauchcha planet's positive potential. The wealth result (rather than simply royal status) suggests that the conjunction-plus-aspect combination particularly activates material abundance over political power, though both outcomes coexist. Immensely wealthy
interpretation.summary: A planet at paramauchcha that is both aspected by and conjunct a friendly planet produces immense wealth (escalation from pd-ch07-033).

condition.description: Planet at paramauchcha + aspected by friendly + conjunct friendly planet

source.original_text: If the Sun is in its own Amsa and the Moon is in its own sign, the person will be a king with horses and elephants.

interpretation.detailed: When the Sun is placed in its own Amsa (Simha Navamsa — the Sun's own sign in the Navamsa chart) and the Moon is in its own sign (Karka/Cancer in the Rasi chart), the native will be a king with horses and elephants. This yoga combines the two luminaries each in positions of maximum dignity: the Sun in its Navamsa-level own sign and the Moon in its Rasi-level own sign. The Sun represents kingship and authority; the Moon represents the mind, public, and mother. Both in own positions create a balanced solar-lunar yoga of power. King with horses and elephants
interpretation.summary: Sun in its own Navamsa division (Simha) and Moon in its own sign (Karka) produces a king with horses and elephants.

condition.description: Sun in Simha Navamsa (own Amsa) AND Moon in Karka (own sign in Rasi)

source.original_text: If the full Moon is in Meena and is aspected by a friendly planet, the person will be a king pre-eminent among kings.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is full and is placed in Meena (Pisces) and receives the aspect of a friendly planet, the native will be a king pre-eminent (foremost) among kings. Meena is the sign of Jupiter's ownership and is considered a spiritually elevated sign. The full Moon in Meena combines lunar completeness with Jovian/spiritual placement. The 'pre-eminent among kings' designation implies a king who surpasses other kings — a paramount sovereign or emperor-equivalent. King pre-eminent among kings
interpretation.summary: A full Moon in Meena (Pisces) receiving a friendly planet's aspect produces a king who is pre-eminent (superior) among all kings.

condition.description: Moon full in Meena + aspected by friendly planet

source.original_text: If the full Moon is in Vrishabha (its sign of exaltation), the person will be a generous and charitable king praised by the good.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is full and placed in Vrishabha (Taurus), its sign of exaltation (highest exaltation at 3° Vrishabha), the native will be a generous and charitable king who is praised by the good (virtuous people). This is the Moon at peak strength in both Paksha Bala (full Moon) and Uchchabala (exaltation). The emphasis on generosity and charity rather than military power suggests the moral and dharmic dimension of this yoga — a king who is not merely powerful but also virtuous and beloved by the righteous. Generous and charitable king praised by the good
interpretation.summary: A full Moon in Vrishabha (its exaltation sign) produces a generous and charitable king praised by virtuous people.

condition.description: Moon full in Vrishabha (exaltation sign)

source.original_text: If the Moon is in a friendly Amsa and is aspected by Venus, the person will be a king possessed of much wealth.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is placed in a friendly Amsa (a divisional chart position owned by a planet friendly to the Moon) and receives the aspect of Venus, the native will be a king possessed of much wealth. The Moon in a friendly Amsa is strong in divisional dignity; Venus's aspect adds material prosperity, beauty, and luxury to the Moon's already positive divisional state. The result emphasises wealth ('much wealth') rather than pure military or political power, reflecting Venus's nature as the planet of affluence and pleasure. King possessed of much wealth
interpretation.summary: Moon in a friendly Amsa (divisional position) aspected by Venus produces a king with much wealth.

condition.description: Moon in friendly Amsa + aspected by Venus

source.original_text: If the Moon is in a friendly Amsa and is aspected by Jupiter, the person will rule the entire earth.

interpretation.detailed: When the Moon is placed in a friendly Amsa and receives the aspect of Jupiter, the native will rule the entire earth. This is the superior variant of pd-ch07-038 (Venus aspect → much wealth). Here, Jupiter's aspect instead of Venus's produces a higher-order outcome: not just a wealthy king but a ruler of the entire earth. Jupiter's aspect carries dharmic wisdom and expansive authority — qualities that translate into universal sovereignty rather than personal wealth. The contrast between pd-ch07-038 and pd-ch07-039 reveals the text's implicit hierarchy: Jupiter's aspect outranks Venus's aspect in terms of sovereign scope. Rules the entire earth
interpretation.summary: Moon in a friendly Amsa aspected by Jupiter produces a native who rules the entire earth.

condition.description: Moon in friendly Amsa + aspected by Jupiter

source.original_text: There result Raja Yogas in the following cases: if malefic planets are in the 3rd, 6th and 11th houses reckoned from the position of the lord of the Lagna or from the Janma Rasi.

interpretation.detailed: When malefic planets (Saturn, Mars, Rahu, Ketu, Sun) occupy the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses counted from either (a) the house where the Lagna lord is placed, or (b) the Janma Rasi (Moon's sign / birth sign), a Raja Yoga results. The 3rd, 6th, and 11th are Upachaya (growth) houses — malefics are considered to thrive and produce good results when placed in these houses. This is one of four named Raja Yoga formations in Sloka 24.
interpretation.summary: Malefic planets in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses counted from the Lagna lord's position or from the Janma Rasi (birth sign) produces a Raja Yoga.

condition.description: Malefics in 3rd/6th/11th from Lagna lord's house position OR from Janma Rasi

source.original_text: If Mars and Mercury are in the 2nd house from the Lagna, there results a Raja Yoga.

interpretation.detailed: When Mars and Mercury are both placed in the 2nd house from the Lagna, a Raja Yoga results. The 2nd house governs wealth, family, speech, and early life. Mars brings energy, drive, and sometimes aggressive speech; Mercury brings intellect, communication, and commerce. Their conjunction in the 2nd is an unusual pairing — Mars and Mercury are considered natural enemies in standard friendship tables, yet their combination in the 2nd is here presented as a positive Raja Yoga. This is one of four named Raja Yoga formations in Sloka 24.
interpretation.summary: Mars and Mercury both in the 2nd house from the Lagna produces a Raja Yoga.

source.original_text: If the Sun and Venus are in the 4th house from the Lagna, there results a Raja Yoga.

interpretation.detailed: When the Sun and Venus are both placed in the 4th house from the Lagna, a Raja Yoga results. The 4th house governs home, mother, landed property, conveyances, and happiness. The Sun (authority, soul, father) and Venus (wealth, beauty, luxury) together in the 4th can indicate great domestic prosperity and authority, or property and vehicles. The Sun and Venus are close enemies in natural friendship tables (their proximity often leads to combust Venus), but when both are in the 4th they activate a Raja Yoga here. This is one of four named Raja Yoga formations in Sloka 24.
interpretation.summary: Sun and Venus both in the 4th house from the Lagna produces a Raja Yoga.

source.original_text: If Mars is in the 10th house, Saturn is in the 11th and Jupiter is in the Lagna, there results a Raja Yoga.

interpretation.detailed: When Mars occupies the 10th house (Digbala position for Mars — directional strength), Saturn occupies the 11th house (an Upachaya house where Saturn is considered to produce good results), and Jupiter occupies the Lagna, a Raja Yoga results. This three-planet specific configuration distributes three important planets across three powerful houses: Mars gains directional strength in the 10th; Saturn gains Upachaya-house benefit in the 11th; Jupiter energises the Ascendant with dharmic wisdom. This is the fourth and most specific named Raja Yoga configuration in Sloka 24.
interpretation.summary: Mars in the 10th house, Saturn in the 11th, and Jupiter in the Lagna together produce a Raja Yoga.

condition.description: Mars in 10th + Saturn in 11th + Jupiter in Lagna (1st house)

source.original_text: Of the lords of the 11th, the 9th, and the 2nd houses, if one is in a Kendra from the Moon and if Jupiter is the lord of the 2nd, 5th or 11th house, the person will be the ruler of a full-blown empire.

interpretation.detailed: When any one of the lords of the 11th, 9th, or 2nd houses is placed in a Kendra house (1/4/7/10) counted from the Moon's position, AND Jupiter is the natural or functional lord of the 2nd, 5th, or 11th house (i.e., the Lagna must be such that Jupiter owns one of these houses — Vrishabha Lagna: Jupiter owns 8th/11th; Karka Lagna: Jupiter owns 6th/9th... the condition is best interpreted as Jupiter's natural lordship of Mithuna/Kanya being excluded, and Dhanus/Meena Lagna where Jupiter owns 1st/4th/10th being most potent), the native will be the ruler of a full-blown empire. The empire-level outcome ('full-blown empire') is the highest political result in this chapter's scale. Ruler of a full-blown empire
interpretation.summary: One of the 11th, 9th, or 2nd house lords in a Kendra from the Moon, with Jupiter ruling the 2nd, 5th, or 11th, produces a ruler of a full-blown empire.

condition.description: One of (11th lord / 9th lord / 2nd lord) in Kendra from Moon AND Jupiter is lord of 2nd/5th/11th

source.original_text: If there is a planet in its sign of depression and if the lord of that sign of depression or the lord of the sign of exaltation of that planet is in a Kendra from the Moon or from the Lagna, the person will be a king and a just ruler.

interpretation.detailed: Neechabhanga Raja Yoga variant 1: When a planet is placed in its sign of depression AND either (a) the lord of that depression sign OR (b) the lord of the sign where that planet would be exalted, is placed in a Kendra from the Moon or from the Lagna, the debilitation is cancelled (Neechabhanga) and the native will be a king and a just ruler. This is the basic (single-lord, OR condition) Neechabhanga: only one of the two lords needs to be in Kendra. This is the weakest of four Neechabhanga variants (see pd-ch07-046, 047, 048 for stronger variants). The 'just ruler' descriptor emphasises dharmic kingship. King and just ruler
interpretation.summary: A debilitated planet with either its depression-sign lord or its exaltation-sign lord in a Kendra from Moon or Lagna produces a king and just ruler (Neechabhanga Raja Yoga, variant 1).

condition.description: Planet in debilitation + (lord of depression sign OR lord of exaltation sign) in Kendra from Moon or Lagna

source.original_text: If the lord of the sign in which a planet is depressed and the lord of the sign of exaltation of that planet are both in mutual Kendras, the person will be an emperor respected by all other kings.

interpretation.detailed: Neechabhanga Raja Yoga variant 2: When a planet is in depression AND both the lord of its depression sign AND the lord of the sign of its exaltation are placed in mutual Kendra positions from each other (not just from Lagna or Moon, but from each other — i.e., they are 1/4/7/10 from one another), the native will be an emperor respected by all other kings. This is a stronger form than variant 1 (pd-ch07-045) because BOTH lords (not just one) must qualify, and they must be in mutual angular relationship. The outcome escalates from 'king and just ruler' (v1) to 'emperor respected by all kings' (v2). Emperor respected by all other kings
interpretation.summary: Both the depression-sign lord and the exaltation-sign lord of a debilitated planet in mutual Kendra positions produces an emperor respected by all kings (Neechabhanga v2).

condition.description: Planet in debilitation + lord of depression sign AND lord of exaltation sign BOTH in mutual Kendra from each other

source.original_text: If a planet in its sign of depression is aspected by the lord of that sign, the person will be a ruler of the earth and famous. If such a planet also occupies an auspicious house, the person will certainly be a foremost king.

interpretation.detailed: Neechabhanga Raja Yoga variant 3: When a planet is in its sign of depression and receives the direct aspect of the lord of that depression sign, the native will be a ruler of the earth and famous. This is the 'aspect cancellation' mechanism for Neechabhanga — the depression-sign lord 'sees' its occupant and effectively redeems it. If this depressed but aspected planet also occupies an auspicious house (Kendra or Trikona), the outcome is amplified: the native will certainly be a foremost king (paramount among kings). The double qualification (aspect + auspicious house) produces the certainty qualifier ('certainly'). Ruler of earth and famous; if in auspicious house — certainly a foremost king
interpretation.summary: A debilitated planet aspected by the lord of its depression sign produces a ruler of earth and fame; additionally in an auspicious house, certainly a foremost king (Neechabhanga v3).

condition.description: Planet in debilitation + aspected by lord of depression sign; optional: also in auspicious house

source.original_text: If the lord of the Rasi occupied by the depressed planet or the lord of the Rasi of exaltation of that planet is in a Kendra from the Lagna or from the Moon, the person will be an emperor possessing full riches; will be virtuously disposed; will be respected by kings; will be mighty; will be famous; and will be affluent.

interpretation.detailed: Neechabhanga Raja Yoga variant 4 (the most elaborately described): When a planet is in its sign of depression AND either the lord of the sign it occupies (the depression sign) OR the lord of the sign of its exaltation is placed in a Kendra from the Lagna or from the Moon, the native will be: an emperor possessing full riches; virtuously disposed; respected by kings; mighty; famous; and affluent. This is structurally similar to variant 1 (pd-ch07-045) — OR condition, one lord in Kendra — but the outcome description is far more detailed and elevated. The elaboration of six specific qualities (riches, virtue, respect, might, fame, affluence) underscores this as the textually climactic Neechabhanga formulation. Note the slight structural overlap with pd-ch07-045; the difference may be in the identity of 'lord of occupied Rasi' (pd-ch07-048 uses the depression-sign lord as 'lord of occupied Rasi') vs pd-ch07-045's explicit 'lord of that sign of depression.' Emperor possessing full riches; virtuously disposed; respected by kings; mighty; famous; affluent
interpretation.summary: A debilitated planet whose occupied Rasi lord or exaltation Rasi lord is in a Kendra from Lagna or Moon produces a wealthy, virtuous, mighty, famous emperor respected by all kings (Neechabhanga v4).

condition.description: Planet in debilitation + (lord of occupied Rasi OR lord of exaltation Rasi) in Kendra from Lagna or Moon

source.original_text: If the Sun be in the 7th house, the person will be wandering, without a wife, and will suffer humiliation.

interpretation.detailed: The Sun placed in the 7th house (Kalatra Bhava) produces a restless, wandering life. The native is deprived of a wife or partner. Humiliation is a noted outcome. Sun, a natural malefic and a significator of authority and pride, sitting in the house of marriage and public relationships produces adverse results for conjugal happiness and social standing. The 7th house also represents the setting Sun in the diurnal arc, symbolically weakening solar qualities in matters of partnership. Wandering, without a wife, suffers humiliation
interpretation.summary: Sun in the 7th house causes the native to wander, remain without a spouse, and suffer humiliation.

source.original_text: If the Sun be in the 8th house, the native loses wealth and friends; he will not be long-lived; and suffers from defective eyesight or becomes blind.

interpretation.detailed: The Sun placed in the 8th house (Ayu Bhava — house of longevity) produces inauspicious outcomes across multiple domains. The native loses both material wealth and social connections (friends). Longevity is diminished — the native is not long-lived. Eyesight suffers — either a defect of vision or complete blindness. The Sun governs the eyes in classical Jyotish, and its placement in the 8th (house of obstacles, chronic illness, and death) afflicts the eyes specifically. The 8th is also considered a dusthana (difficult house), making a natural malefic like the Sun particularly inauspicious here. Loses wealth and friends; not long-lived; defective eyesight or blind
interpretation.summary: Sun in the 8th house causes loss of wealth and friends, shortened lifespan, and defective or lost eyesight.

source.original_text: If the Sun be in the 9th house, the native loses his father; but he will have children and relations and will revere Gods and Brahmins.

interpretation.detailed: The Sun placed in the 9th house (Dharma Bhava) produces a mixed outcome. The native loses their father — the Sun being the karaka of the father is injured in the 9th (father's house), creating early separation or death of the father. However, positive outcomes include having children and extended family relations. The native develops a devout character, revering Gods and Brahmins — this is a natural expression of Sun in the Dharma Bhava, which governs religion, piety, and righteous conduct. The loss of the father is the shadow; the spiritual and family dimensions are the light. Loses father; has children and relations; reveres Gods and Brahmins
interpretation.summary: Sun in the 9th house causes early loss of father but grants children, family relations, and a devout, dharmic disposition.

source.original_text: If the Sun be in the 10th house, the native will have sons, vehicles, laudation, intelligence, wealth, strength, fame; he will be a King.

interpretation.detailed: The Sun placed in the 10th house (Karma Bhava) produces the most elevated possible outcome for solar placement. The Sun gains directional strength (dig bala) in the 10th house, which amplifies all its significations. The native achieves kingly status or authority equivalent to a king. He possesses sons, vehicles, praise and laudation from society, high intelligence, wealth, physical strength, and widespread fame. This is classically considered one of the strongest placements for the Sun in the entire horoscope. The 10th house represents the Sun at its zenith — solar energy expressed at maximum worldly power. Sons, vehicles, laudation, intelligence, wealth, strength, fame; becomes a King
interpretation.summary: Sun in the 10th house, its directional strength (dig bala) house, produces royal authority, fame, wealth, intelligence, sons, and vehicles.
